title: Dynamics of global mpox epidemics, 1970-2025: a systematic review and meta-analysis of evolving transmissibility and intervention effects.
abstract: BACKGROUND: The 2022 global mpox epidemic declined before modified Vaccinia Ankara-Bavarian Nordic (MVA-BN) vaccines were widely deployed, contributing to the perception that transmission was self-limiting within a small high-risk population. This may have delayed global vaccine allocation and weakened responses to the resurgence that has disproportionately affected Africa since 2024. The reasons for the 2022 decline remain uncertain, and prior studies have reported widely divergent estimates of vaccination impact. We systematically reviewed and meta-analysed the evolving transmissibility of mpox clades and the effects of interventions. METHODS: We searched GenBank, PubMed and Embase through 18 May 2025, for mpox virus sequences, reproduction number (R) estimates and modelling studies evaluating intervention effectiveness. Two reviewers independently assessed eligibility, extracted data and evaluated risk of bias using a validated tool. Random-effects meta-analyses were performed. RESULTS: Fifty-two studies reporting R estimates and 40 studies evaluating intervention effectiveness met eligibility criteria. For clade I mpox, pooled R increased from 0.71 (95% CI 0.26 to 1.17) during 1970-2017 to 1.23 (1.12-1.33) for subclades Ib/Ia after 2023 (p=0.0303). For clade II mpox, pooled R was 1.11 (0.90-1.32) during 2017-2021 and increased to 2.66 (2.31-3.00) for subclade IIb in 2022-2023 (p<0.0001). During the 2022 subclade IIb outbreak, empirical modelling studies estimated that behaviour change and vaccination together were associated with a substantial reduction in mpox cases (55%, 95% CI 37 to 73; I2=81.2%), although effect sizes varied across settings according to the extent of behaviour change and the timing and coverage of vaccine rollout. CONCLUSIONS: Behaviour change and vaccination likely played important roles in the decline of the 2022 mpox epidemic in many studied settings. Given the stepwise increase in human-to-human transmissibility associated with the emergence of new subclades, effective mpox epidemic control requires proactive, rapid and equitable vaccine rollout supported by culturally tailored risk communication. PROSPERO REGISTRATION NUMBER: CRD420250653072.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on the dynamics of global mpox epidemics from 1970 to 2025, examining the evolving transmissibility of mpox clades and the effects of interventions. The central question is whether behavior change and vaccination have played significant roles in controlling mpox outbreaks, particularly during the 2022 epidemic and subsequent resurgence in Africa.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The evidence base includes mpox virus sequences, reproduction number (R) estimates, and modeling studies evaluating intervention effectiveness. The review searched GenBank, PubMed, and Embase through 18 May 2025. Two reviewers independently assessed eligibility, extracted data, and evaluated risk of bias using a validated tool. Random-effects meta-analyses were performed to synthesize findings.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The pooled reproduction number (R) for clade I mpox increased from 0.71 (95% CI 0.26 to 1.17) during 1970-2017 to 1.23 (1.12-1.33) for subclades Ib/Ia after 2023. analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Effective mpox epidemic control requires proactive, rapid, and equitable vaccine rollout, supported by culturally tailored risk communication. The review emphasizes the need for further research on the mechanisms of increased transmissibility in new subclades and the optimization of intervention strategies across different settings.

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review and meta-analysis investigate the dynamics of global mpox epidemics from 1970 to 2025, focusing on the evolving transmissibility of mpox clades and the impact of interventions. The review highlights a significant increase in the reproduction number (R) for clade IIb mpox, particularly in 2022-2023, compared to earlier periods. It also reports that behavior change and vaccination were associated with a substantial reduction in mpox cases during the 2022 outbreak, though effect sizes varied by setting. The findings underscore the importance of rapid and equitable vaccine distribution, supported by culturally appropriate risk communication, to control mpox epidemics. The review identifies uncertainties in the reasons for the 2022 decline and calls for further research on the mechanisms of increased transmissibility in new subclades.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 本综述关注1970年至2025年全球猴痘疫情的动态,研究猴痘分支的传播力变化以及干预措施的效果。核心问题是行为改变和疫苗接种是否在控制猴痘疫情,尤其是在2022年疫情及随后非洲的疫情反弹中发挥了重要作用。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 证据基础包括猴痘病毒序列、繁殖数(R)估计值以及评估干预效果的建模研究。本综述于2025年5月18日通过GenBank、PubMed和Embase进行检索。两名评审员独立评估了资格、提取数据并使用经过验证的工具评估偏倚风险。进行了随机效应荟萃分析以综合研究结果。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 分支簇I 猴痘 的汇总再生数(R)从1970-2017年的0.71(95% CI 0.26至1.17)上升至2023年后亚分支簇Ib/Ia的1.23(1.12-1.33)。分支簇II 猴痘 在2017-2021年间的R为1.11(0.90-1.32),而在2022-2023年亚分支簇IIb则升至2.66(2.31-3.00)。实证模型研究估计,行为改变与疫苗接种 共同使2022年亚分支簇IIb 暴发 期间的猴痘 病例减少了55%(95% CI 37至73),但效应规模在不同环境中存在差异。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 2022年猴痘病例下降的原因仍不确定,先前研究对疫苗接种的影响估计差异很大。证据还突出了干预效果的异质性,这受到行为改变程度以及疫苗部署的时间和覆盖范围的影响。对于新亚分支传播力增加的确切机制尚无共识。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 有效的猴痘疫情控制需要由文化定制的风险沟通支持的主动、快速和公平的疫苗部署。本综述强调需要进一步研究新亚分支传播力增加的机制以及在不同环境中优化干预策略。

abstract_zh: 背景:2022年全球猴痘疫情在改良型牛痘病毒-巴伐利亚北(MVA-BN)疫苗广泛部署之前出现下降,这导致人们认为传播在小规模高风险人群中具有自限性。这可能延迟了全球疫苗的分配,并削弱了对自2024年以来主要影响非洲的疫情反弹的应对。2022年疫情下降的原因仍不确定,先前研究对疫苗接种的影响估计差异很大。我们系统综述并荟萃分析了猴痘分支的传播力变化以及干预措施的效果。方法:我们于2025年5月18日通过GenBank、PubMed和Embase检索了猴痘病毒序列、繁殖数(R)估计值和评估干预效果的建模研究。两名评审员独立评估了资格、提取数据并使用经过验证的工具评估偏倚风险。进行了随机效应荟萃分析。结果:有52项研究报告了R估计值,40项研究评估了干预效果,符合纳入标准。对于I型猴痘分支,合并后的R值从1970年至2017年的0.71(95% CI 0.26至1.17)上升至2023年后Ib/Ia亚分支的1.23(1.12-1.33)(p=0.0303)。对于II型猴痘分支,合并后的R值在2017年至2021年为1.11(0.90-1.32),而在2022年至2023年的IIb亚分支中上升至2.66(2.31-3.00)(p<0.0001)。在2022年IIb亚分支暴发期间,实证建模研究估计,行为改变和疫苗接种共同作用导致猴痘病例显著减少(55%,95% CI 37至73;I2=81.2%),尽管不同环境下的效应大小因行为改变的程度以及疫苗部署的时间和覆盖范围而有所不同。结论:在许多研究环境中,行为改变和疫苗接种可能在2022年猴痘疫情下降中发挥了重要作用。鉴于新亚分支出现与人传人传播力逐步增加相关,有效的猴痘疫情控制需要由文化定制的风险沟通支持的主动、快速和公平的疫苗部署。PROSPERO注册号:CRD420250653072。

analysis_zh.scope_and_question: 本综述关注1970年至2025年全球猴痘疫情的动态,研究猴痘分支的传播力变化以及干预措施的效果。核心问题是行为改变和疫苗接种是否在控制猴痘疫情,尤其是在2022年疫情及随后非洲的疫情反弹中发挥了重要作用。
analysis_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 证据基础包括猴痘病毒序列、繁殖数(R)估计值以及评估干预效果的建模研究。本综述于2025年5月18日通过GenBank、PubMed和Embase进行检索。两名评审员独立评估了资格、提取数据并使用经过验证的工具评估偏倚风险。进行了随机效应荟萃分析以综合研究结果。
analysis_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 分支簇I 猴痘 的汇总再生数(R)从1970-2017年的0.71(95% CI 0.26至1.17)上升至2023年后亚分支簇Ib/Ia的1.23(1.12-1.33)。分支簇II 猴痘 在2017-2021年间的R为1.11(0.90-1.32),而在2022-2023年亚分支簇IIb则升至2.66(2.31-3.00)。实证模型研究估计,行为改变与疫苗接种 共同使2022年亚分支簇IIb 暴发 期间的猴痘 病例减少了55%(95% CI 37至73),但效应规模在不同环境中存在差异。
analysis_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 2022年猴痘病例下降的原因仍不确定,先前研究对疫苗接种的影响估计差异很大。证据还突出了干预效果的异质性,这受到行为改变程度以及疫苗部署的时间和覆盖范围的影响。对于新亚分支传播力增加的确切机制尚无共识。
analysis_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 有效的猴痘疫情控制需要由文化定制的风险沟通支持的主动、快速和公平的疫苗部署。本综述强调需要进一步研究新亚分支传播力增加的机制以及在不同环境中优化干预策略。

title: Prevalence of mpox infection among men who have sex with men: a systematic review and meta-analysis
abstract: Abstract Background Mpox has been twice declared as public health emergency of international concern by World Health Organization. The 2022–2024 global outbreak has been primarily driven by sexual transmission within men who have sex with men (MSM) networks, predominantly involving Clade IIb, with a subsequent surge of Clade Ib in early 2024. MSM account for a large proportion of confirmed mpox cases. This review aimed to estimate the prevalence of mpox infection among MSM populations. Methods We searched PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, China National Knowledge Infrastructure (CNKI) and Wanfang Data for studies published in English or Chinese from inception to 16 December 2024. Eligible studies reported mpox cases among MSM with confirmed diagnosis (laboratory or self-reported) during the outbreak period. Reviews, case reports, and studies without case numbers were excluded. American Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality and Newcastle-Ottawa Scale were adopted for quality assessment. Fixed-effects or random-effects meta-analysis was performed to estimate the pooled prevalence of mpox among MSM. Heterogeneity was measured using Cochran's Q test and I 2 statistics. Meta regression analysis was performed to discover the potential source of the heterogeneity. Funnel plot, Egger's regression test and Begg's rank correlation test were conducted to evaluate the publication bias. Sensitivity analyses were performed by leave-one-out analysis and by stratified validation. Results From 1606 retrieved studies, 28 studies were eligible and included, containing a total of 46,598 MSM participants and 1274 mpox cases from 15 countries. The pooled mpox prevalence among MSM population was 2.30% [95% confidence interval ( CI ): 1.29–3.57%]. Meta-regression identified continent as the most significant moderator, with prevalence in South America (9.58, 95% CI : 2.71–20.01%) being significantly higher than in Asia (1.14, 95% CI : 0.56–1.90%) ( P = 0.019). Sampling method also contributed to the heterogeneity, whereas no statistically significant difference was observed in mpox prevalence among high-risk MSM, asymptomatic MSM, comparing to the general MSM populations respectively. Conclusions This study confirms a significant but highly heterogeneous burden of mpox among MSM worldwide. The findings suggest that the observed prevalence is shaped more by regional epidemiological contexts and study methodologies, which emphasizes the necessity for geographically prioritized interventions and standardizing surveillance to enable accurate risk assessment and guide resource allocation in future outbreaks.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review aimed to estimate the prevalence of mpox infection among men who have sex with men (MSM) populations globally, focusing on the role of sexual transmission and the impact of different clades of the mpox virus.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The evidence base included 28 studies retrieved from PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, China National Knowledge Infrastructure (CNKI), and Wanfang Data, covering studies published in English or Chinese from inception to 16 December 2024. The review used fixed-effects or random-effects meta-analysis to estimate pooled prevalence, with heterogeneity assessed using Cochran's Q test and I 2 statistics. Meta-regression was conducted to identify potential sources of heterogeneity, and publication bias was evaluated using funnel plots, Egger's regression test, and Begg's rank correlation test. Sensitivity analyses were performed via leave-one-out and stratified validation methods.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The pooled prevalence of mpox among MSM was estimated at 2.30% [95% confidence interval (CI): 1.29–3.57%]. Meta-regression identified continent as the most significant moderator, with South America showing a significantly higher prevalence (9.58, 95% CI: 2.71–20.01%) compared to Asia (1.14, 95% CI: 0.56–1.90%) (P = 0.019). The study concluded that mpox prevalence among MSM is significant but highly heterogeneous, influenced by regional epidemiological contexts and study methodologies.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review noted that sampling methods contributed to heterogeneity, but no statistically significant difference in prevalence was observed among high-risk MSM, asymptomatic MSM, or general MSM populations. There is a lack of clarity on the exact mechanisms driving the surge in Clade Ib cases in early 2024, and the study did not provide detailed insights into the biological or ecological factors behind the regional variations in prevalence.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The findings highlight the need for geographically prioritized interventions and standardized surveillance to enable accurate risk assessment and guide resource allocation in future outbreaks. The review suggests that future research should focus on understanding the epidemiological and ecological factors contributing to the regional variations in mpox prevalence among MSM, as well as the role of different clades in transmission dynamics.

analysis_en.scope_and_question: The review aimed to estimate the prevalence of mpox infection among men who have sex with men (MSM) populations globally, focusing on the role of sexual transmission and the impact of different clades of the mpox virus.
analysis_en.evidence_base_and_review_method: The evidence base included 28 studies retrieved from PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, China National Knowledge Infrastructure (CNKI), and Wanfang Data, covering studies published in English or Chinese from inception to 16 December 2024. The review used fixed-effects or random-effects meta-analysis to estimate pooled prevalence, with heterogeneity assessed using Cochran's Q test and I 2 statistics. Meta-regression was conducted to identify potential sources of heterogeneity, and publication bias was evaluated using funnel plots, Egger's regression test, and Begg's rank correlation test. Sensitivity analyses were performed via leave-one-out and stratified validation methods.
analysis_en.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The pooled prevalence of mpox among MSM was estimated at 2.30% [95% confidence interval (CI): 1.29–3.57%]. Meta-regression identified continent as the most significant moderator, with South America showing a significantly higher prevalence (9.58, 95% CI: 2.71–20.01%) compared to Asia (1.14, 95% CI: 0.56–1.90%) (P = 0.019). The study concluded that mpox prevalence among MSM is significant but highly heterogeneous, influenced by regional epidemiological contexts and study methodologies.
analysis_en.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review noted that sampling methods contributed to heterogeneity, but no statistically significant difference in prevalence was observed among high-risk MSM, asymptomatic MSM, or general MSM populations. There is a lack of clarity on the exact mechanisms driving the surge in Clade Ib cases in early 2024, and the study did not provide detailed insights into the biological or ecological factors behind the regional variations in prevalence.
analysis_en.research_and_practice_implications: The findings highlight the need for geographically prioritized interventions and standardized surveillance to enable accurate risk assessment and guide resource allocation in future outbreaks. The review suggests that future research should focus on understanding the epidemiological and ecological factors contributing to the regional variations in mpox prevalence among MSM, as well as the role of different clades in transmission dynamics.

title_zh: 男性同性性行为中猴痘感染的患病率:系统综述和荟萃分析
source_body_en: Abstract Background Mpox has been twice declared as public health emergency of international concern by World Health Organization. The 2022–2024 global outbreak has been primarily driven by sexual transmission within men who have sex with men (MSM) networks, predominantly involving Clade IIb, with a subsequent surge of Clade Ib in early 2024. MSM account for a large proportion of confirmed mpox cases. This review aimed to estimate the prevalence of mpox infection among MSM populations. Methods We searched PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, China National Knowledge Infrastructure (CNKI) and Wanfang Data for studies published in English or Chinese from inception to 16 December 2024. Eligible studies reported mpox cases among MSM with confirmed diagnosis (laboratory or self-reported) during the outbreak period. Reviews, case reports, and studies without case numbers were excluded. American Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality and Newcastle-Ottawa Scale were adopted for quality assessment. Fixed-effects or random-effects meta-analysis was performed to estimate the pooled prevalence of mpox among MSM. Heterogeneity was measured using Cochran's Q test and I 2 statistics. Meta regression analysis was performed to discover the potential source of the heterogeneity. Funnel plot, Egger's regression test and Begg's rank correlation test were conducted to evaluate the publication bias. Sensitivity analyses were performed by leave-one-out analysis and by stratified validation. Results From 1606 retrieved studies, 28 studies were eligible and included, containing a total of 46,598 MSM participants and 1274 mpox cases from 15 countries. The pooled mpox prevalence among MSM population was 2.30% [95% confidence interval ( CI ): 1.29–3.57%]. Meta-regression identified continent as the most significant moderator, with prevalence in South America (9.58, 95% CI : 2.71–20.01%) being significantly higher than in Asia (1.14, 95% CI : 0.56–1.90%) ( P = 0.019). Sampling method also contributed to the heterogeneity, whereas no statistically significant difference was observed in mpox prevalence among high-risk MSM, asymptomatic MSM, comparing to the general MSM populations respectively. Conclusions This study confirms a significant but highly heterogeneous burden of mpox among MSM worldwide. The findings suggest that the observed prevalence is shaped more by regional epidemiological contexts and study methodologies, which emphasizes the necessity for geographically prioritized interventions and standardizing surveillance to enable accurate risk assessment and guide resource allocation in future outbreaks.

title: Mpox Airborne Transmission: A Systematic Review.
abstract: Since May 2022, mpox has been reported across multiple nonendemic regions, with concurrent outbreaks in diverse geographic settings, raising concerns about broader international spread. However, evidence regarding the risk of airborne transmission remains limited. We conducted a systematic review to evaluate the risk of airborne transmission and the presence of viable viruses in air samples. PubMed, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library were searched for studies published in English, including environmental studies, case reports, cross-sectional studies, and cohort studies. Data extraction included study characteristics (authors, year, design, and setting), sample size, diagnostic methods, participant characteristics, follow-up, type of respiratory particles assessed (droplets and/or aerosols), and key findings. Of 286 records identified, four studies met the inclusion criteria. All were environmental studies published between 2022 and 2023. MPXV DNA was detected in surface and air samples, with cycle threshold (Ct) values ranging from < 30 to < 45. However, none of the studies demonstrated consistent viral viability in aerosols or droplets sufficient to support airborne transmission. Overall, the available evidence is limited and does not support a clear risk of airborne infection. Further well-designed studies in human settings are needed to clarify the potential for mpox transmission through respiratory routes. SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: PROSPERO: CRD42023391123.

title_zh: 猴痘 机载 传播:系统回顾。
source_body_en: Since May 2022, mpox has been reported across multiple nonendemic regions, with concurrent outbreaks in diverse geographic settings, raising concerns about broader international spread. However, evidence regarding the risk of airborne transmission remains limited. We conducted a systematic review to evaluate the risk of airborne transmission and the presence of viable viruses in air samples. PubMed, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library were searched for studies published in English, including environmental studies, case reports, cross-sectional studies, and cohort studies. Data extraction included study characteristics (authors, year, design, and setting), sample size, diagnostic methods, participant characteristics, follow-up, type of respiratory particles assessed (droplets and/or aerosols), and key findings. Of 286 records identified, four studies met the inclusion criteria. All were environmental studies published between 2022 and 2023. MPXV DNA was detected in surface and air samples, with cycle threshold (Ct) values ranging from < 30 to < 45. However, none of the studies demonstrated consistent viral viability in aerosols or droplets sufficient to support airborne transmission. Overall, the available evidence is limited and does not support a clear risk of airborne infection. Further well-designed studies in human settings are needed to clarify the potential for mpox transmission through respiratory routes. SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: PROSPERO: CRD42023391123.

title: Saliva and Oropharyngeal Swabs as Screening Tools for Mpox: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis
abstract: Objectives: The global mpox outbreak that began in 2020 was declared a public health emergency of international concern in 2024. However, there is limited scientific evidence regarding the use of salivary and/or oropharyngeal swab samples to detect the virus. In this review, we systematically examined existing literature to evaluate the potential of saliva and/or oropharyngeal swab samples as screening tools for mpox detection. Methods: The final analysis included 15 articles comprising 2,610 participants, including mpox-infected individuals (polymerase chain reaction confirmed) whose saliva and/or oropharyngeal samples (OPSs) tested positive for the virus. After a quality assessment, a random-effects model with logit transformation was used to pool the positivity rates. Results: The pooled positivity rate of mpox virus DNA was 76.7% (95% confidence interval [CI], 27.9%–96.6%) in saliva and 69.7% (95% CI, 40.1%–88.8%) in OPSs. The high heterogeneity between the studies (I 2 = 99.5%) for both specimen types was addressed through sensitivity analyses. The median shedding durations were 19 and 21 d for saliva and OPSs, respectively. Conclusions: The high positivity rates and sustained shedding in saliva and OPSs indicate that these methods can serve as noninvasive, adjunct, early-phase alternatives for rapid mpox detection, supporting enhanced surveillance, outbreak monitoring, and global public health preparedness. Knowledge Transfer Statement: The findings of this systematic review are directly relevant to clinicians, dental surgeons, and infection control specialists in understanding the diagnostic value of saliva and oropharyngeal samples for mpox. This knowledge can aid in screening, infection control, and patient management within health care settings.

The review includes 15 studies with 2,610 participants, focusing on polymerase chain reaction-confirmed mpox cases. title: Monkeypox Virus Surveillance — United States, 2024–2025
abstract: Since the onset of a global outbreak of monkeypox virus (MPXV) infections in 2022, cases have declined substantially in the United States; however, ongoing low-level transmission has persisted. To assess trends in cases of MPXV infection in the United States during 2024-2025, investigators analyzed data from the One CDC Data Platform and the National Notifiable Diseases Surveillance System. In 2024, a total of 2,803 cases of MPXV infection were reported in the United States, including one travel-associated clade Ib case. In 2025, a total of 2,519 cases were reported, including 10 clade Ib cases. The number of reported cases of MPXV infection during September-October 2025 was double that during the same period in 2024, although cases returned to background levels by the end of December 2025. Demographic characteristics of patients with MPXV infections, including distributions by sex, race and ethnicity, sexual orientation, lesion location, and age, were similar to those reported in previous years. Among 860 patients with complete information, the odds of hospitalization among those who were unvaccinated were 9.73 times those who were fully vaccinated when controlling for age group and HIV status. Encouraging completion of the recommended 2-dose vaccination series for persons at risk for MPXV exposure, including travelers to specific countries with ongoing clade I or clade II transmission, could reduce the risk for severe illness and hospitalization. Continued routine surveillance remains important to limiting future spread, monitoring changes in viral evolution, and focusing vaccination efforts on affected areas.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addressed the need to characterize ongoing low-level transmission of monkeypox virus (MPXV) in the United States after a global outbreak in 2022, despite substantial declines in cases.
analysis.study_design_and_population: Investigators analyzed surveillance data from the One CDC Data Platform and the National Notifiable Diseases Surveillance System for MPXV infections reported in the United States during 2024–2025.
analysis.methods: The analysis included case counts, demographic distributions, clade typing, and an assessment of vaccination status in relation to hospitalization outcomes using adjusted odds ratios.
analysis.main_results: In 2024, 2,803 MPXV cases were reported, including one travel-associated clade Ib case, while in 2025, 2,519 cases were reported, including 10 clade Ib cases. Cases in September–October 2025 were double those in the same period in 2024 but returned to background levels by December 2025. Among 860 patients with complete data, the odds of hospitalization were 9.73 times higher in unvaccinated individuals compared with those fully vaccinated after adjusting for age group and HIV status.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the resurgence of clade Ib cases and the doubling of late-2025 cases as evidence of ongoing transmission requiring sustained surveillance and targeted vaccination.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings support prioritizing completion of the 2-dose vaccination series for persons at risk, including travelers to areas with clade I or II transmission, to reduce severe illness and hospitalization.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study relies on passive surveillance data, which may undercount cases and lacks detailed clinical or genomic data for all reported cases, limiting causal inference and generalizability.

analysis.summary_en: This MMWR report analyzed U.S. monkeypox virus (MPXV) surveillance data from 2024–2025 to assess trends after the 2022 global outbreak. In 2024, 2,803 cases were reported, including one travel-associated clade Ib case, while 2025 saw 2,519 cases, including 10 clade Ib cases. Cases in September–October 2025 were double those in the same period in 2024 but returned to background levels by December 2025. Among 860 patients with complete data, unvaccinated individuals had 9.73 times higher odds of hospitalization compared with fully vaccinated individuals after adjusting for age and HIV status. The authors highlight the need for continued routine surveillance and completion of the 2-dose vaccination series for at-risk groups, including travelers to areas with ongoing clade I or II transmission.

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 研究人员分析了2024–2025年美国报告的猴痘病毒感染病例数据,数据来源于“One CDC数据平台”和“国家法定报告疾病监测系统”。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在在2022年全球猴痘病毒暴发后,尽管美国病例数大幅下降,但仍需表征该国猴痘病毒的持续低水平传播现状。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 研究人员分析了2024–2025年美国报告的猴痘病毒感染病例数据,数据来源于“One CDC数据平台”和“国家法定报告疾病监测系统”。
analysis_zh.methods: 分析包括病例数量、人口学分布、分支分型以及评估疫苗接种状况与住院结局的关联(使用调整后的优势比)。
analysis_zh.main_results: 2024年共报告2,803例猴痘病毒感染病例,其中包括1例与旅行相关的Ib分支病例;2025年共报告2,519例病例,其中包括10例Ib分支病例。2025年9–10月报告的病例数是2024年同期的两倍,但截至2025年12月底,病例数已回落至背景水平。在860名信息完整的患者中,未接种疫苗者的住院风险是完全接种疫苗者的9.73倍(在控制年龄组和HIV感染状况后)。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将Ib分支病例的再次出现以及2025年末病例数的倍增解释为持续传播的证据,表明需要持续监测和针对性疫苗接种。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果支持优先完成针对猴痘病毒暴露风险人群(包括赴正在流行I或II分支猴痘病毒的特定国家的旅行者)推荐的2剂疫苗接种,以减少重症和住院风险。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究依赖被动监测数据,可能低估病例数量,且缺乏所有报告病例的详细临床或基因组数据,限制了因果推断和结果的普遍性。

title: Emerging infectious diseases (Mpox, Nipah, and Andes): A narrative review of transmission, environmental survival, and disinfection
abstract: BACKGROUND: Mpox, Nipah virus, and Andes virus are emerging infectious diseases that cause outbreaks associated with nosocomial transmission. METHODS: This narrative review summarizes the Mpox, Nipah virus, and Andes virus epidemiology, clinical manifestations, diagnosis, and treatment with a focus on environmental survival, susceptibility to antiseptics and disinfectants, and infection prevention. RESULTS: Mpox, Nipah virus, and Andes virus all survive in the environment and are capable of indirect transmission. All these viruses are enveloped and susceptible to commonly used antiseptics and surface disinfectants. CONCLUSIONS: Rapid identification of patients with known or suspected infections of these emerging viruses coupled with adherence to infection prevention recommendations will prevent healthcare-associated transmission.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review examines Monkeypox virus (MPXV), including mpox disease, its clades (clade I, clade II, clade Ib), and associated outbreaks with a focus on nosocomial transmission and infection prevention in healthcare settings.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: This narrative review synthesizes epidemiology, clinical features, diagnosis, treatment, environmental survival, susceptibility to antiseptics and disinfectants, and infection prevention strategies for MPXV and related orthopoxviruses.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: MPXV demonstrates environmental survival and indirect transmission potential, and as an enveloped virus, it remains susceptible to commonly used antiseptics and surface disinfectants.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The supplied evidence does not report heterogeneity in environmental survival across MPXV clades, nor does it provide comparative data on disinfectant efficacy specifically stratified by clade or environmental conditions.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Rapid identification of patients with suspected mpox and strict adherence to infection prevention recommendations are critical to preventing healthcare-associated transmission of MPXV.

title_zh: 新发传染病(猴痘、尼帕病毒和安第斯山脉):传播、环境生存和消毒的叙述性回顾
source_body_en: BACKGROUND: Mpox, Nipah virus, and Andes virus are emerging infectious diseases that cause outbreaks associated with nosocomial transmission. METHODS: This narrative review summarizes the Mpox, Nipah virus, and Andes virus epidemiology, clinical manifestations, diagnosis, and treatment with a focus on environmental survival, susceptibility to antiseptics and disinfectants, and infection prevention. RESULTS: Mpox, Nipah virus, and Andes virus all survive in the environment and are capable of indirect transmission. All these viruses are enveloped and susceptible to commonly used antiseptics and surface disinfectants. CONCLUSIONS: Rapid identification of patients with known or suspected infections of these emerging viruses coupled with adherence to infection prevention recommendations will prevent healthcare-associated transmission.
abstract_zh: 背景:猴痘、尼帕病毒和安第斯病毒是新出现的传染病,导致与医院 传播 相关的 暴发。方法:这篇叙述性综述总结了 猴痘、尼帕病毒和安第斯病毒 流行病学、临床表现、诊断 和 治疗,重点是环境生存、对防腐剂和消毒剂的敏感性以及感染预防。结果:猴痘、尼帕病毒和安第斯病毒都可以在环境中生存,并且能够间接感染 传播。所有这些病毒都有包膜,对常用的防腐剂和表面消毒剂敏感。结论:快速识别已知或疑似感染这些新出现病毒的患者,并遵守感染预防建议,将预防与医疗保健相关的 传播。

title: Clade-specific multiplex digital PCR assay for monkeypox virus detection in spike-in wastewater samples.
abstract: Monkeypox virus (MPXV) is a zoonotic pathogen that has recently caused outbreaks in non-endemic areas. Wastewater-based surveillance is independent of individual testing and offers substantial potential for monitoring population-level disease dynamics of MPXV at the clade level, as clades differ in transmissibility and mortality rate. Here, we report the validation of a four-plex digital PCR assay to detect and quantify the major clades and subclades of MPXV. The assay demonstrated strong linearity, analytical sensitivity (limits of detection ranged from 6.7 to 9.6 copies per reaction across targets) and specificity in distinguishing and quantifying MPXV by clade, which is advantageous for both clinical and wastewater applications.

analysis.summary_en: This study presents a clade-specific multiplex digital PCR assay for detecting and quantifying monkeypox virus (MPXV) in wastewater samples. title_zh: 猴痘病毒分支特异性多重数字PCR检测方法在废水样本中的验证
source_body_en: Monkeypox virus (MPXV) is a zoonotic pathogen that has recently caused outbreaks in non-endemic areas. Wastewater-based surveillance is independent of individual testing and offers substantial potential for monitoring population-level disease dynamics of MPXV at the clade level, as clades differ in transmissibility and mortality rate. Here, we report the validation of a four-plex digital PCR assay to detect and quantify the major clades and subclades of MPXV. The assay demonstrated strong linearity, analytical sensitivity (limits of detection ranged from 6.7 to 9.6 copies per reaction across targets) and specificity in distinguishing and quantifying MPXV by clade, which is advantageous for both clinical and wastewater applications.

title: Dermoscopic Features of Mpox: A Case Series
abstract: ABSTRACT Monkeypox (mpox) is a viral infection characterized by polymorphic cutaneous lesions and systemic symptoms, including fever, lymphadenopathy, headache and myalgia. Given its broad differential diagnosis, accurate recognition requires a high level of clinical suspicion; in this context, dermoscopy represents a potentially useful tool to improve diagnostic accuracy. We conducted a retrospective case series of six patients with RT‐PCR–confirmed mpox and dermatologic involvement between July 2022 and July 2025. A total of six patients were included; three (50%) were evaluated in the macular/vesicular phase and three (50%) in the crusted phase. In the macular/vesicular phase, eight lesions were analysed. In the crusted phase, five lesions were analysed. In our series, we observed pinkish‐yellow structureless areas during the macular/vesicular phase. Recognition of these dermoscopic features may increase clinical suspicion and support the diagnosis.

title: Evaluating U.S. Federal Zoonotic Records Against National One Health Goals: A Multi-LLM Assessment Across COVID-19, Mpox, and H5N1
abstract: (1) Background: Zoonotic diseases require coordinated action across human, animal, and environmental health sectors. While substantial research has focused on outbreak prediction, forecasting, and surveillance, less attention has been given to systematically evaluating how One Health principles are reflected in government policy documents. (2) Methods: We developed a multi–large language model (LLM) framework to evaluate 477 U.S. government documents covering COVID-19, mpox, and highly pathogenic avian influenza (H5N1). Agency technical guidance and Federal Register documents were evaluated using a 19-item rubric covering three goals of the U.S. National One Health Framework: coordination and communication, outbreak response, and surveillance. Claude, GPT, and Gemini independently evaluated the documents, with agreement assessed using Fleiss’ κ and independent human validation. (3) Results: One Health alignment was generally limited, with no disease × document-type × goal combination exceeding 39%. Document type showed the clearest differences: agency technical guidance had 13 to 30 percentage-point higher alignment than Federal Register documents for coordination and outbreak response, respectively (both p < 0.001). Differences across diseases were less consistent. After excluding one wording-sensitive rubric item, the three LLMs reached unanimous agreement in 87.1% of document-item evaluations. Human–model agreement (Cohen’s κ = 0.513–0.692) was comparable to human–human agreement (κ = 0.649). (4) Conclusions: Three main findings emerged: document type showed clearer differences in One Health alignment than disease or publication period; clearer and more operational criteria supported more consistent evaluation; and multi-LLM consensus showed strong reproducibility for scalable policy assessment. Together, these findings extend zoonotic-disease research beyond outbreak prediction and surveillance toward systematic evaluation of One Health policy.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to evaluate how well U.S. federal zoonotic records align with the National One Health goals, particularly in the context of mpox, by examining the reflection of these principles in government policy documents.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study involved a multi-LLM framework to assess 477 U.S. government documents related to mpox, COVID-19, and H5N1. These documents included agency technical guidance and Federal Register entries.
analysis.methods: The evaluation used a 19-item rubric to assess alignment with three One Health goals: coordination and communication, outbreak response, and surveillance. The three LLMs (Claude, GPT, and Gemini) independently analyzed the documents, with agreement measured using Fleiss’ κ and validated by human reviewers.
analysis.main_results: One Health alignment was generally limited, with no disease × document-type × goal combination exceeding 39%. analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study found that document type had a more significant impact on One Health alignment than disease or publication period. analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that systematic evaluation of One Health policy documents can improve coordination across sectors and enhance the operationalization of policy goals for zoonotic diseases like mpox.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluates the alignment of U.S. federal zoonotic records with the National One Health goals, focusing on mpox. Using a multi-LLM framework, it analyzed 477 government documents, including agency technical guidance and Federal Register entries. The results showed limited One Health alignment, with document type having the clearest differences. The study highlights the importance of operational criteria in policy evaluation and the reproducibility of multi-LLM consensus. These findings suggest that systematic policy assessment can improve intersectoral coordination for zoonotic diseases. However, the study's reliance on LLMs introduces potential biases, though human validation supports moderate confidence in the results.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在评估美国联邦人兽共患病记录与‘国家一体化健康’目标的符合程度,重点关注猴痘背景下政府政策文件中‘一体化健康’原则的体现情况。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究采用多大语言模型框架,评估了477份美国政府文件,涵盖猴痘、COVID-19与H5N1。文件类型包括机构技术指导文件与《联邦公报》条目。
elements_zh.methods: 评估采用包含19个评分项的量表,涵盖‘一体化健康’的三大目标:协调与沟通、暴发应对与监测。Claude、GPT与Gemini三个模型独立分析文件,采用Fleiss κ系数评估一致性,并由人工审核员进行验证。
elements_zh.main_results: 整体‘一体化健康’对齐程度有限,无任何疾病×文件类型×目标组合的对齐率超过39%。文件类型差异最为显著:在协调与暴发应对方面,机构技术指导文件的对齐率分别比《联邦公报》文件高13至30个百分点(p值均<0.001)。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究发现,文件类型对‘一体化健康’对齐程度的影响较疾病或发布时间更显著。研究还指出,更清晰与可操作的评估标准可提升评估一致性,且多大语言模型共识在可扩展政策评估中表现出较强的可重复性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,系统性评估‘一体化健康’政策文件可提升跨部门协调,并强化人兽共患病(如猴痘)政策目标的可操作性。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究基于多大语言模型框架,可能存在解释偏倚。但模型间高度一致性及人工验证结果支持研究结论的中等可信度。

abstract_zh: (1) 背景:人兽共患病需要在人类、动物与环境健康部门间开展协调行动。尽管大量研究聚焦于暴发预测、预报与监测,但针对政府政策文件中‘一体化健康’原则体现情况的系统性评估关注较少。(2) 方法:本研究构建多大语言模型(LLM)框架,评估了477份美国政府文件,涵盖COVID-19、猴痘与高致病性禽流感(H5N1)。采用包含19个评分项的评估量表,对美国‘国家一体化健康框架’的三大目标进行评估:协调与沟通、暴发应对与监测。Claude、GPT与Gemini三个模型独立评估文件,采用Fleiss κ系数评估一致性,并由人工进行独立验证。(3) 结果:整体‘一体化健康’对齐程度有限,无任何疾病×文件类型×目标组合的对齐率超过39%。文件类型差异最为显著:在协调与暴发应对方面,机构技术指导文件的对齐率分别比《联邦公报》文件高13至30个百分点(p值均<0.001)。疾病间差异不一致。在排除一项对措辞敏感的评分项后,三个LLM在87.1%的文件-评分项评估中达成一致。人类-模型一致性(Cohen κ=0.513–0.692)与人类-人类一致性(κ=0.649)相当。(4) 结论:研究得出三项主要发现:文件类型在‘一体化健康’对齐程度上较疾病或发布时间更显著;更清晰与可操作的评估标准可提升一致性;多LLM共识在可扩展政策评估中表现出较强的可重复性。这些发现将人兽共患病研究从暴发预测与监测扩展至‘一体化健康’政策的系统性评估。

title: Multiomics profiling of plasma reveals lipid-immune dysregulation and exosome remodeling in mpox and mpox-HIV co-infection.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Monkeypox virus (MPXV) infects diverse human cell types, and human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) co-infection is common. The immunometabolic consequences of MPXV infection, and how it may be altered by HIV, remain poorly defined. METHODS: We performed quantitative plasma lipidomics and precise metabolomics in a discovery cohort (n = 81) comprising MPXV-monoinfected (MPLWOH), MPXV-HIV-coinfected (MPLWH), and HIV-monoinfected (PLWH) patients and healthy controls, integrating exosome proteomics, cytokine profiling, and transcriptomics of exosome-treated HepG2 and A549 cells for functional interpretation. An independent validation cohort (n = 65) was used to assess cross-cohort reproducibility. FINDINGS: MPXV infection induced broad lipid remodeling, with elevations in phosphatidylserine (PS) and phosphatidylethanolamine (PE) and reductions in phosphatidylcholine (PC), lysophospholipids, cholesteryl ester (CE), and exosomal lecithin-cholesterol acyltransferase (LCAT) and lipoprotein lipase (LPL). These lipid alterations were correlated with tissue injury markers and inflammatory cytokines. The MPLWH group exhibited more severe metabolic disruption, including marked sulfatide (SL) depletion, lower cholesterol and high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL-c), and extensive rewiring of lipid-cytokine associations. SL depletion in MPLWH correlated with abundances of COPI-mediated retrograde trafficking proteins in exosomes. Transcriptomic profiling of exosome-treated cells provided functional validation: MPLWOH exosomes induced lipid metabolism and repair-associated epithelial programs, while MPLWH exosomes drove phospholipid remodeling and acute inflammatory and mucosal barrier-stress responses. CONCLUSIONS: MPXV infection reprograms host lipid metabolism and exosome composition, with HIV co-infection amplifying inflammatory, metabolic, and trafficking disruptions. These convergent multi-omics signatures link systemic lipid dysregulation to exosome-mediated immunomodulation and identify potential targets for host-directed interventions. FUNDING: This study was funded by the Major Project of Guangzhou National Laboratory.

abstract_zh: 背景:猴痘病毒(MPXV)感染多种人类细胞类型,且人类免疫缺陷病毒(HIV)共感染较为常见。MPXV感染的免疫代谢后果以及HIV如何改变这些过程仍不明确。方法:我们在一项发现队列研究(n = 81)中进行了定量血浆脂质组学和精确代谢组学分析,该队列包括MPXV单感染(MPLWOH)、MPXV-HIV共感染(MPLWH)和HIV单感染(PLWH)患者以及健康对照组,并整合了外泌体蛋白组学、细胞因子谱分析以及外泌体处理的HepG2和A549细胞的转录组学数据,以进行功能解释。独立验证队列研究(n = 65)用于评估跨队列研究的可重复性。发现:MPXV感染导致广泛的脂质重塑,表现为磷脂酰丝氨酸(PS)和磷脂酰乙醇胺(PE)升高,而磷脂酰胆碱(PC)、溶血磷脂、胆固醇酯(CE)以及外泌体中的卵磷脂胆固醇乙酰转移酶(LCAT)和脂蛋白脂肪酶(LPL)水平降低。这些脂质变化与组织损伤标志物和炎症细胞因子相关。MPLWH组表现出更严重的代谢紊乱,包括显著的硫酸脑苷脂(SL)减少、胆固醇和高密度脂蛋白胆固醇(HDL-c)水平降低,以及脂质-细胞因子关联的广泛重塑。MPLWH组中SL的减少与外泌体中COPI介导的逆行运输蛋白的丰度相关。外泌体处理细胞的转录组学分析提供了功能验证:MPLWOH外泌体诱导与脂质代谢和修复相关的上皮程序,而MPLWH外泌体则驱动磷脂重塑及急性炎症和黏膜屏障应激反应。结论:MPXV感染重新编程了宿主的脂质代谢和外泌体组成,HIV共感染则放大了炎症、代谢和运输的紊乱。这些一致的多组学特征将系统性脂质失调与外泌体介导的免疫调节联系起来,并指出了针对宿主的潜在干预靶点。资助:本研究由广州国家实验室重大专项资助。

title: Monkeypox virus clade IIb isolate exhibits reduced virulence relative to clade IIa isolates in multiple murine models
abstract: ABSTRACT Monkeypox virus (MPXV) is the causative agent of mpox disease in humans. The virus comprises two clades, Central African clade I and West African clade II, with case fatality rates of ~11 and ~4%, respectively. Since the discovery of mpox disease in 1970, the virus has been restricted to Africa. However, in 2022, a previously unrecognized subclade IIb caused the largest global outbreak of mpox disease with a case fatality rate of ~0.2%. The difference in virulence of MPXV subclades in human infection warrants further investigation; however, one critical limitation is the lack of susceptible small animal models. In this study, we investigated the susceptibility of four murine models, including CAST-EiJ and three immunocompromised models (C57BL/6 Ifnar −/− , C57BL/6 Ifngr −/− , and C57BL/6 Ifnar −/− / Ifngr −/− ) to MPXV clade IIa (WR 7-61 and US-2003) and IIb (MA-2022) isolates. All four mouse models were susceptible to clade IIa infection, leading to severe disease marked by decreased body temperature, weight loss, and lethality. In contrast, clade IIb infection produced minimal to mild disease at similar doses in all four murine models. The clade IIb isolate produced severe disease (40% lethality) at only the highest dose (8.0 log 10 PFU) in the most susceptible immunocompromised mouse model, C57BL/6 Ifnar −/− / Ifngr −/− . This is the first demonstration of lethal disease with clade IIb in a murine model. In addition, these data show that clade IIa is ~100 to 100,000-fold more virulent than clade IIb and provides three additional murine models for investigating MPXV infection and pathogenesis. IMPORTANCE Mpox is an emerging human disease caused by four distinct MPXV subclades (Ia, Ib, IIa, and IIb). Despite genetic similarities, the case fatality rate varies considerably between the subclades: Ia (~11%), Ib and IIa (~4%), and IIb (~0.2%). Since 2022, multiple mpox outbreaks have occurred due to previously unrecognized subclades, leading to the declaration of two public health emergencies by the World Health Organization. This unprecedented global spread, coupled with the variation in the severity of human disease, underscores the importance of research into the pathogenesis of emerging MPXV subclades. However, a critical limitation is the lack of suitable small animal models. This study identifies three additional murine models susceptible to MPXV clade II infection and demonstrates significant virulence differences between clades IIa and IIb. These models will enable a rapid characterization of previously unrecognized subclades and will facilitate countermeasure development.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Mpox is an emerging human disease caused by distinct Monkeypox virus (MPXV) subclades with widely varying case fatality rates, yet the virulence differences between subclades remain insufficiently understood due to the lack of suitable small animal models.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study evaluated susceptibility of four murine models—CAST-EiJ and three immunocompromised strains (C57BL/6 Ifnar −/− , C57BL/6 Ifngr −/− , and C57BL/6 Ifnar −/− / Ifngr −/− )—to MPXV clade IIa (WR 7-61 and US-2003) and clade IIb (MA-2022) isolates.
analysis.methods: The authors infected mice with standardized doses of clade IIa and IIb isolates and monitored disease progression through clinical signs including body temperature, weight loss, and lethality.
analysis.main_results: All four mouse models developed severe disease after clade IIa infection, whereas clade IIb infection produced minimal to mild disease at similar doses; only the most immunocompromised model (C57BL/6 Ifnar −/− / Ifngr −/− ) showed 40% lethality at the highest clade IIb dose (8.0 log10 PFU).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings demonstrate clade IIa is approximately 100- to 100,000-fold more virulent than clade IIb in murine models and provide the first lethal clade IIb infection in mice, identifying three new models for MPXV research.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These murine models enable rapid characterization of emerging MPXV subclades and facilitate countermeasure development, addressing a critical gap in mpox research infrastructure.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its exclusive use of murine models, which may not fully recapitulate human disease, and by the absence of data on clade Ib or clade I isolates, reducing generalisability to all MPXV subclades.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated virulence differences between Monkeypox virus (MPXV) clade IIa and clade IIb isolates using four murine models. All models were susceptible to clade IIa infection, resulting in severe disease and lethality, whereas clade IIb infection produced minimal to mild disease at comparable doses. Only the most immunocompromised C57BL/6 Ifnar −/− / Ifngr −/− mice exhibited 40% lethality at the highest clade IIb dose, demonstrating clade IIa is approximately 100- to 100,000-fold more virulent than clade IIb. The work provides the first lethal clade IIb infection in mice and identifies three new murine models for MPXV research, enabling rapid characterization of emerging subclades and countermeasure development.

elements_zh.methods: 作者使用标准化剂量感染小鼠,并通过包括体温下降、体重减轻和死亡在内的临床症状监测疾病进展。
elements_zh.main_results: 所有四种小鼠模型在感染IIa分支后均表现出严重疾病,而IIb分支感染在相似剂量下仅引起轻微至轻度疾病;仅在最易感的免疫缺陷小鼠模型C57BL/6 Ifnar −/− / Ifngr −/− 中,IIb分支分离株在最高剂量(8.0 log10 PFU)下导致了40%的死亡率。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,在小鼠模型中,IIa分支的致病性大约是IIb分支的100到100,000倍,并首次在小鼠中观察到IIb分支的致死性感染,识别了三种新的MPXV研究模型。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些小鼠模型能够快速表征新兴的MPXV亚分支,并促进应对措施的开发,填补了猴痘病研究基础设施中的关键空白。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究的局限性在于仅使用了小鼠模型,这可能无法完全模拟人类疾病,且缺乏对IIb或I分支分离株的数据,限制了其对所有MPXV亚分支的普遍适用性。

analysis_en.research_question_and_background: Mpox is an emerging human disease caused by distinct Monkeypox virus (MPXV) subclades with widely varying case fatality rates, yet the virulence differences between subclades remain insufficiently understood due to the lack of suitable small animal models.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: The study evaluated susceptibility of four murine models—CAST-EiJ and three immunocompromised strains (C57BL/6 Ifnar −/− , C57BL/6 Ifngr −/− , and C57BL/6 Ifnar −/− / Ifngr −/− )—to MPXV clade IIa (WR 7-61 and US-2003) and clade IIb (MA-2022) isolates.
analysis_en.methods: The authors infected mice with standardized doses of clade IIa and IIb isolates and monitored disease progression through clinical signs including body temperature, weight loss, and lethality.
analysis_en.main_results: All four mouse models developed severe disease after clade IIa infection, whereas clade IIb infection produced minimal to mild disease at similar doses; only the most immunocompromised model (C57BL/6 Ifnar −/− / Ifngr −/− ) showed 40% lethality at the highest clade IIb dose (8.0 log10 PFU).
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings demonstrate clade IIa is approximately 100- to 100,000-fold more virulent than clade IIb in murine models and provide the first lethal clade IIb infection in mice, identifying three new models for MPXV research.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These murine models enable rapid characterization of emerging MPXV subclades and facilitate countermeasure development, addressing a critical gap in mpox research infrastructure.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its exclusive use of murine models, which may not fully recapitulate human disease, and by the absence of data on clade Ib or clade I isolates, reducing generalisability to all MPXV subclades.

title_zh: 猴痘病毒IIb分支分离株在多种小鼠模型中表现出比IIa分支分离株更低的致病性
source_body_en: ABSTRACT Monkeypox virus (MPXV) is the causative agent of mpox disease in humans. The virus comprises two clades, Central African clade I and West African clade II, with case fatality rates of ~11 and ~4%, respectively. Since the discovery of mpox disease in 1970, the virus has been restricted to Africa. However, in 2022, a previously unrecognized subclade IIb caused the largest global outbreak of mpox disease with a case fatality rate of ~0.2%. The difference in virulence of MPXV subclades in human infection warrants further investigation; however, one critical limitation is the lack of susceptible small animal models. In this study, we investigated the susceptibility of four murine models, including CAST-EiJ and three immunocompromised models (C57BL/6 Ifnar −/− , C57BL/6 Ifngr −/− , and C57BL/6 Ifnar −/− / Ifngr −/− ) to MPXV clade IIa (WR 7-61 and US-2003) and IIb (MA-2022) isolates. All four mouse models were susceptible to clade IIa infection, leading to severe disease marked by decreased body temperature, weight loss, and lethality. In contrast, clade IIb infection produced minimal to mild disease at similar doses in all four murine models. The clade IIb isolate produced severe disease (40% lethality) at only the highest dose (8.0 log 10 PFU) in the most susceptible immunocompromised mouse model, C57BL/6 Ifnar −/− / Ifngr −/− . This is the first demonstration of lethal disease with clade IIb in a murine model. In addition, these data show that clade IIa is ~100 to 100,000-fold more virulent than clade IIb and provides three additional murine models for investigating MPXV infection and pathogenesis. IMPORTANCE Mpox is an emerging human disease caused by four distinct MPXV subclades (Ia, Ib, IIa, and IIb). Despite genetic similarities, the case fatality rate varies considerably between the subclades: Ia (~11%), Ib and IIa (~4%), and IIb (~0.2%). Since 2022, multiple mpox outbreaks have occurred due to previously unrecognized subclades, leading to the declaration of two public health emergencies by the World Health Organization. This unprecedented global spread, coupled with the variation in the severity of human disease, underscores the importance of research into the pathogenesis of emerging MPXV subclades. However, a critical limitation is the lack of suitable small animal models. This study identifies three additional murine models susceptible to MPXV clade II infection and demonstrates significant virulence differences between clades IIa and IIb. These models will enable a rapid characterization of previously unrecognized subclades and will facilitate countermeasure development.

title: MPOX: ASPECTOS GERAIS E O USO DA ABORDAGEM ONE HEALTH NO CONTEXTO DESSA ZOONOSE VIRAL MPOX: GENERAL ASPECTS AND THE USE OF THE ONE HEALTH APPROACH IN THE CONTEXT OF THIS VIRAL ZOONOSIS MPOX: ASPECTOS GENERALES Y USO DEL ENFOQUE UNA SOLA SALUD EN EL CONTEXTO DE ESTA ZOONOSIS VIRAL
abstract: A Mpox é uma zoonose viral emergente de distribuição global, causada pelo Monkeypox vírus (MPXV), pertencente ao gênero Orthopoxvirus. O presente estudo teve como objetivo descrever de forma breve e pontual as principais características da Mpox e apresentar informações sobre o uso da abordagem One Health como forma de enfrentamento a essa zoonose. Trata-se de uma revisão narrativa da literatura, com seleção de publicações realizadas entre 2014 e 2025, utilizando as bases de dados LILACS, SciELO, PubMed e Google Acadêmico. Além disso, documentos de órgãos oficiais nacionais e internacionais foram pesquisados no contexto do estudo. O MPXV é um vírus de DNA de fita dupla, identificado inicialmente em animais em 1958 e em humanos na década de 1970, apresentando dois clados com potencial para causar infecções. Clinicamente, a Mpox manifesta-se em fases prodrômica e eruptiva, caracterizadas por febre, linfadenopatia e lesões cutâneas. A transmissão ocorre principalmente por contato direto com lesões e secreções, sendo o diagnóstico confirmado por PCR. O manejo da doença inclui cuidados relacionados aos sintomas e tratamento das complicações secundárias. A abordagem One Health, ao integrar ações entre saúde humana, animal e ambiental, torna-se relevante no contexto dessa zoonose. A Mpox apresenta relação com fatores comportamentais e sociais, impactando grupos específicos, necessitando de medidas de prevenção e políticas públicas efetivas. A cooperação interdisciplinar e o fortalecimento da vigilância epidemiológica são fundamentais para o controle efetivo da Mpox a partir da abordagem One Health.

analysis.summary_en: This study provides an overview of the Mpox virus, highlighting its status as a globally emerging viral zoonosis caused by MPXV, a member of the Orthopoxvirus genus. The research aims to briefly describe the main characteristics of Mpox and emphasize the importance of the One Health approach in addressing this zoonosis. The study is a narrative literature review of publications from 2014 to 2025, sourced from databases such as LILACS, SciELO, PubMed, and Google Scholar, along with official documents. It outlines that transmission occurs primarily through direct contact with lesions and secretions, and diagnosis is confirmed via PCR. Clinically, Mpox presents in prodromic and eruptive phases, marked by fever, lymphadenopathy, and skin lesions. The findings suggest that Mpox is linked to behavioral and social factors, affecting specific groups and requiring effective prevention measures and public policies. The One Health approach is deemed essential for managing the disease by integrating human, animal, and environmental health actions. The study acknowledges the need for interdisciplinary cooperation and strengthened epidemiological surveillance for effective control. However, it does not provide detailed statistical or methodological limitations, which may affect the strength of the evidence.

title: Enhancing Interpretability for Automated Human Monkeypox Skin Lesions Detection Using Pre-trained Transfer Learning Networks
abstract: Abstract Identification of skin lesions remains a challenging task because of low image contrast, large variations in disease manifestations, and strong visual similarities among dermatological conditions. Deep transfer learning (TL)-integrated artificial intelligence (AI) systems offer an effective solution for rapid and accurate computer-aided diagnosis of multiple infectious skin diseases. In this study, a TL-based framework is proposed as an automated human monkeypox (MP) skin lesion detection (HMSLD) for monkeypox (MP), chickenpox (CP), measles (MS), and normal skin lesion classification. A publicly available dataset comprising 654 RGB clinical images. The HMSLD performed image preprocessing, data augmentation, class imbalance handling through inverse class weighting, and comparative analysis of pre-trained TL models, namely Xception, ResNet152V2, NASNetLarge, EfficientNetB0, EfficientNetB7, MobileNetV2, and MobileNetV3. MobileNetV3 performed best among the models. Their overall performance with an accuracy = 91%, precision = 91%, recall = 89%, F1-score = 90%, and an AUROC of 0.99, indicating excellent discriminative capability. MobileNetV3 achieved 96% precision for measles and 100% recall for normal skin, while EfficientNetB0 performed the highest precision at 96% and an F1-score of 93%. MobileNetV3 provides the most balanced trade-off among the evaluated models between classification accuracy, robustness, and computational efficiency. These evaluated performances indicate the potential of the HMSLD framework. It may be a reliable and cost-effective computer-aided diagnostic tool for early MP screening and other clinically similar skin diseases.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, India Section A: Physical Sciences

title: Finger-actuated microfluidic device for point-of-care circulating cell-free nucleic acid extraction.
abstract: Timely and accurate nucleic acid extraction is a critical bottleneck in point-of-care (POC) molecular diagnostics, particularly for low-abundance cell-free nucleic acids (DNA, RNA, miRNA) in plasma. We present a fully finger-actuated microfluidic device for power-free, pipette-free, nucleic acid extraction. The prototype device integrates finger-actuated valves, pump and blister reagent storage, enabling a complete, intuitive, "sample-to-eluate" workflow, including lysis, binding, washing and elution via manual actuation in approximately 35 minutes. The device operation was benchmarked against a commercial magnetic bead-based manual benchtop and an automated robotic workflow. In DNA-spiked aqueous samples (5-20 ng mL -1 ), the device demonstrated recoveries of 84.6%, against 90.7% on the bench. Optimisation of magnetic bead volume identified 50 μL as the threshold for maximal recovery while minimising reagent consumption. Recovery from human pooled plasma samples were found to be on average 18, 62, and 552% higher than that obtained with the control bench extraction on initial sample volumes of 100, 75 and 50 μL, respectively. Coefficient of variation (CV%) for all techniques remained within reported laboratory ranges (20-80%). The device's clinical utility was piloted using patient samples positive for cytomegalovirus (CMV), monkeypox virus (MPXV) or chikungunya (CHIKV). The device achieved successful qPCR amplification for all targets, with viral DNA Cq values within as little as 0.3 cycles of the standard protocol. This instrument-free, manual circulating nucleic acid extraction tool could help bridge the gap between lateral flow based nucleic acid amplification technologies and real-world decentralised diagnostics, offering a scalable solution for infectious disease management in resource-limited settings.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addresses the critical need for rapid, accessible nucleic acid extraction at the point of care to enable decentralised molecular diagnostics, particularly for low-abundance circulating cell-free nucleic acids in clinical samples.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The authors developed and evaluated a finger-actuated microfluidic device designed for power-free, pipette-free nucleic acid extraction with a manual, instrument-free workflow.
analysis.methods: The device integrates finger-actuated valves, a pump, and blister-based reagent storage to perform lysis, binding, washing, and elution in approximately 35 minutes, and was benchmarked against commercial magnetic bead-based manual and automated robotic workflows.
analysis.main_results: In DNA-spiked aqueous samples (5–20 ng mL−1), the device achieved 84.6% recovery compared to 90.7% for the bench control, while in human pooled plasma, recoveries were 18%, 62%, and 552% higher than the bench extraction at initial volumes of 100, 75, and 50 μL, respectively.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret the device as enabling a scalable, decentralised solution for nucleic acid extraction that maintains performance close to standard protocols, with clinical utility demonstrated by successful qPCR amplification from patient samples positive for cytomegalovirus, monkeypox virus, or chikungunya.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The device could bridge the gap between lateral flow nucleic acid amplification technologies and decentralised diagnostics, supporting infectious disease management in resource-limited settings where infrastructure and power are constrained.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is limited to proof-of-concept and pilot testing with small sample sizes and abstract-level data, indicating moderate strength and the need for larger, controlled clinical evaluations to confirm performance and generalisability.

analysis.summary_en: This study introduces a finger-actuated microfluidic device designed to enable power-free, pipette-free nucleic acid extraction for point-of-care diagnostics. The device integrates manual actuation for lysis, binding, washing, and elution in a 35-minute workflow and was benchmarked against commercial magnetic bead-based methods. In DNA-spiked samples, recovery was 84.6% versus 90.7% for the bench control, while in plasma, recoveries exceeded bench extraction by 18% to 552% depending on sample volume. title_zh: 指动式微流控设备用于即时检测循环无细胞核酸提取
source_body_en: Timely and accurate nucleic acid extraction is a critical bottleneck in point-of-care (POC) molecular diagnostics, particularly for low-abundance cell-free nucleic acids (DNA, RNA, miRNA) in plasma. We present a fully finger-actuated microfluidic device for power-free, pipette-free, nucleic acid extraction. The prototype device integrates finger-actuated valves, pump and blister reagent storage, enabling a complete, intuitive, "sample-to-eluate" workflow, including lysis, binding, washing and elution via manual actuation in approximately 35 minutes. The device operation was benchmarked against a commercial magnetic bead-based manual benchtop and an automated robotic workflow. In DNA-spiked aqueous samples (5-20 ng mL -1 ), the device demonstrated recoveries of 84.6%, against 90.7% on the bench. Optimisation of magnetic bead volume identified 50 μL as the threshold for maximal recovery while minimising reagent consumption. Recovery from human pooled plasma samples were found to be on average 18, 62, and 552% higher than that obtained with the control bench extraction on initial sample volumes of 100, 75 and 50 μL, respectively. Coefficient of variation (CV%) for all techniques remained within reported laboratory ranges (20-80%). The device's clinical utility was piloted using patient samples positive for cytomegalovirus (CMV), monkeypox virus (MPXV) or chikungunya (CHIKV). The device achieved successful qPCR amplification for all targets, with viral DNA Cq values within as little as 0.3 cycles of the standard protocol. This instrument-free, manual circulating nucleic acid extraction tool could help bridge the gap between lateral flow based nucleic acid amplification technologies and real-world decentralised diagnostics, offering a scalable solution for infectious disease management in resource-limited settings.

title: Epidemiology, Pathophysiology and Clinical Presentation of Pandemics Over the Last Three Decades: A Critical Narrative Review of the Evidence Base for Prevention, Control and Management
abstract: Pandemics and pandemic-scale emergencies of the past three decades have produced an unusually large and heterogeneous body of evidence, yet the epidemiological, mechanistic and clinical literatures have largely developed in parallel and have rarely been appraised together. This review examines that literature critically, taking as its material the human immunodeficiency virus pandemic, the 2003 severe acute respiratory syndrome epidemic, the 2009 influenza A(H1N1) pandemic, Middle East respiratory syndrome, the West African and Congolese Ebola virus disease epidemics, the Zika virus epidemic, the ongoing seventh cholera pandemic, coronavirus disease 2019, the multi-country mpox emergencies, and the panzootic spread of highly pathogenic avian influenza A(H5N1). Literature was identified through searches of three openly accessible bibliographic resources and selected institutional sources, with all bibliographic records verified against registry metadata. The synthesis identifies four persistent problems. First, the operational category of a pandemic remains unstable, which affects the timing of declarations, the comparability of burden estimates and the allocation of resources. Second, the principal epidemiological quantities used to guide policy, including reproduction numbers, case fatality ratios and excess mortality, are estimated by methods whose assumptions are frequently unstated and whose disagreements are substantial enough to alter conclusions. Third, mechanistic accounts of severe disease have converged on a small number of shared processes, in particular innate immune dysregulation, endothelial injury and immunothrombosis, but the inferential basis for these accounts rests heavily on cross-sectional and post-mortem material from severely ill patients in high-income settings. Fourth, evidence on countermeasures is markedly stratified, with randomised evidence for vaccines and several therapeutics but predominantly observational and model-based evidence for non-pharmaceutical interventions. Confidence is strongest for the age gradient of severity, for the efficacy of several vaccine platforms and for the existence of a substantial post-acute symptom burden, and weakest for the comparative effectiveness of individual non-pharmaceutical interventions and for the mechanistic basis of post-acute syndromes. Research priorities that follow from these findings concern standardised burden estimation, prospective mechanistic cohorts recruited across the severity spectrum, and pre-agreed trial infrastructure capable of producing interpretable results during the acute phase of an emergency.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on the epidemiology, pathophysiology, and clinical presentation of pandemics over the last three decades, with a particular emphasis on the mpox virus. It aims to critically evaluate the evidence base for prevention, control, and management strategies related to mpox and other similar viruses.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review synthesizes literature from three openly accessible bibliographic resources and selected institutional sources. All bibliographic records were verified against registry metadata. The review is a critical narrative synthesis rather than a systematic or meta-analytic review, as it does not explicitly report on pooled estimates or standardized methodologies for data analysis.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review identifies four persistent problems in the literature: the instability of the operational category of a pandemic, the lack of standardized methods for estimating key epidemiological quantities, the reliance on cross-sectional and post-mortem data for mechanistic accounts of severe disease, and the stratification of evidence on countermeasures. Confidence is strongest for the age gradient of severity, the efficacy of several vaccine platforms, and the existence of a substantial post-acute symptom burden.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: There is significant controversy regarding the operational definition of a pandemic, which affects the timing of declarations, comparability of burden estimates, and resource allocation. Additionally, the evidence on the comparative effectiveness of individual non-pharmaceutical interventions and the mechanistic basis of post-acute syndromes is weak. The review also highlights a lack of prospective mechanistic cohorts across the severity spectrum.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Research priorities include standardizing burden estimation methods, recruiting prospective mechanistic cohorts across the severity spectrum, and establishing pre-agreed trial infrastructure capable of producing interpretable results during the acute phase of an emergency. These priorities aim to improve the understanding of mpox and enhance the effectiveness of prevention, control, and management strategies.

analysis.summary_en: This review critically examines the epidemiology, pathophysiology, and clinical presentation of mpox virus and related pandemics over the last three decades. It identifies key challenges in the evidence base, including the instability of pandemic definitions, inconsistent estimation methods for epidemiological quantities, reliance on limited data for mechanistic insights, and stratified evidence on countermeasures. The review emphasizes the need for standardized burden estimation, prospective mechanistic studies, and pre-agreed trial infrastructure to improve the management of mpox and similar viruses. Confidence is strongest for the age gradient of severity, vaccine efficacy, and post-acute symptom burden, but weaker for non-pharmaceutical interventions and mechanistic explanations of post-acute syndromes.

abstract_zh: 过去三十年中的大流行及大流行级别紧急事件产生了数量庞大且异质性显著的证据体系,但流行病学、发病机制与临床文献却鲜少交叉评估,且多以平行方式发展。本综述对该文献进行批判性审视,以人类免疫缺陷病毒大流行为材料,并涵盖2003年严重急性呼吸综合征疫情、2009年甲型H1N1流感大流行、中东呼吸综合征、西非与刚果埃博拉病毒病疫情、寨卡病毒疫情、第七次霍乱大流行、2019冠状病毒病、多国XQTERMAFQXZ紧急事件以及高致病性禽流感A(H5N1)泛动物症传播。文献检索基于三个开放获取书目资源及选定机构来源,所有书目记录均与注册元数据进行核验。综述识别出四个持续存在的问题。第一,大流行的操作性定义仍不稳定,影响了宣布时机、负担估算的可比性及资源分配。第二,指导政策的主要流行病学量化指标(包括基本再生数、病例死亡率及超额XQTERMRQXZ)的估算方法假设常未明示,且不同方法间的分歧足以改变结论。第三,重症发病机制的解释已收敛于少数共享过程,特别是先天免疫失调、内皮损伤与免疫血栓形成,但这些解释的推理基础主要依赖于来自高收入地区重症患者的横断面与尸检材料。第四,对防控措施的证据呈现显著分层,抗病毒药物与若干治疗手段的随机证据较为充分,而非药物干预措施则主要依赖观察性研究与模型证据。信心水平最高的领域包括:严重程度的年龄梯度、若干疫苗平台的有效性以及显著的发病后症状负担;信心水平最低的领域则包括:单项非药物干预措施的比较有效性及发病后综合征的发病机制基础。基于上述发现,研究优先事项包括:标准化负担估算、在严重程度谱系上前瞻性招募机制研究队列以及在紧急事件急性期内能够产出可解释结果的预先商定试验基础设施。

title: Sexually Transmitted Infections of the Colon—Clinical Picture, Endoscopic Features, and Laboratory Diagnosis: A Practical Review for the General Practitioner
abstract: Sexually transmitted infections (STIs) are common and probably underreported causes of proctitis and colitis. Bacterial (chlamydia, gonorrhoea, syphilis, Mycoplasma genitalium), viral (herpes simplex virus, mpox), and amoebic (Entamoeba histolytica) pathogens can cause inflammatory proctitis or colitis, which, depending on the pathogen, can mimic inflammatory bowel disease both on endoscopy and histopathology. Rectal and colonic masses are uncommon, but important manifestations of these infections, especially with chlamydia, syphilis, and E. Testing for HIV is important in this context, since it allows for the inclusion of opportunistic pathogens into the differential diagnosis. Chronic diarrhoea can be a feature of chronic HIV infection. Enteric pathogens, such as Salmonella spp., Shigella spp., or Campylobacter spp., can be transmitted during sex, especially during oral–anal contact (“rimming”). The most common STI, human papillomavirus, is not associated with colitis, but is important because of its causal association with genital warts and anal cancer.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review examines sexually transmitted infections (STIs) that can cause proctitis or colitis, with a central question on the clinical, endoscopic, and laboratory features of these infections, including mpox virus (MPXV) as a viral cause. The scope excludes non-target pathogens unless target-specific evidence is present.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a narrative synthesis without explicit systematic review methods, databases, search dates, or eligibility criteria reported. It synthesizes general clinical and diagnostic features of STIs, including mpox, without meta-analytic or consensus processes.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that mpox virus is a recognized viral cause of proctitis or colitis, contributing to inflammatory presentations that may mimic inflammatory bowel disease. It also notes that rectal and colonic masses are uncommon but important manifestations of infections, including those caused by mpox.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review does not provide detailed comparative data or resolve controversies specific to mpox virus. It lacks granular evidence on diagnostic accuracy, treatment efficacy, or mechanistic pathways for mpox-associated colitis. The role of mpox clades in disease severity or presentation is not addressed.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review implies that clinicians should include mpox virus in the differential diagnosis of proctitis or colitis, particularly in patients with risk factors for STIs. It suggests that testing for mpox and other STI pathogens is essential for accurate diagnosis and management.

analysis.summary_en: This review synthesizes clinical, endoscopic, and laboratory features of sexually transmitted infections (STIs) causing proctitis or colitis, with a focus on mpox virus (MPXV) as a viral etiology. It highlights that mpox can present with inflammatory proctitis or colitis, sometimes mimicking inflammatory bowel disease, and notes that rectal or colonic masses are uncommon but clinically significant manifestations. The review emphasizes the importance of including mpox in differential diagnoses for patients with relevant risk factors. However, it lacks systematic methods, pooled estimates, or detailed comparative data specific to mpox. Key gaps include unresolved diagnostic accuracy, treatment efficacy, and mechanistic insights for mpox-associated colitis.

abstract_zh: 性传播感染(STIs)是直肠炎和结肠炎的常见且可能被低估的病因。细菌(衣原体、淋病奈瑟菌、梅毒螺旋体、生殖支原体)、病毒(单纯疱疹病毒、猴痘病毒)、阿米巴(溶组织内阿米巴)等病原体可引起炎症性直肠炎或结肠炎,其内镜与组织病理学表现可在不同病原体间模拟炎症性肠病。直肠与结肠肿块罕见,但作为这些感染的重要临床表现,在衣原体、梅毒与大肠杆菌感染中尤为突出。在此背景下,HIV检测至关重要,因其可将机会性病原体纳入鉴别诊断范围。慢性腹泻可为慢性HIV感染的特征。沙门菌属、志贺菌属或弯曲杆菌属等肠道病原体可通过性传播途径传播,尤其是在口-肛接触(“舔肛”)过程中。最常见的STI——人乳头瘤病毒——与结肠炎无关,但因其可引起生殖器疣与肛门癌而备受关注。

analysis_zh.scope_and_question: 本综述探讨可引起直肠炎或结肠炎的性传播感染(STIs),核心问题聚焦于这些感染的临床、内镜与实验室特征,包括猴痘病毒(MPXV)作为病毒性病因。本综述范围不涵盖非目标病原体,除非存在针对目标病原体的特定证据。
analysis_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 本综述为叙述性综合,未报告明确的系统性综述方法、数据库、检索日期或纳入标准。其综合了STIs的一般临床与诊断特征,包括猴痘病毒,但未进行荟萃分析或共识流程。

analysis_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 本综述未提供猴痘病毒的详细对比数据或解决相关争议。在猴痘病毒诊断准确性、特考韦瑞疗效或猴痘病毒相关结肠炎发病机制等方面缺乏细粒度证据。猴痘病毒分支在疾病严重程度或临床表现中的作用亦未涉及。
analysis_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 本综述暗示临床医师应将猴痘病毒纳入直肠炎或结肠炎的鉴别诊断范围,尤其在存在STIs风险因素的患者中。其建议对猴痘病毒与其他STIs病原体进行检测,以实现准确诊断与治疗。

title: Strengthening Infectious Disease Surveillance in Nigeria: A Focused Scoping Review of SORMAS and the Electronic Integrated Disease Surveillance and Response System
abstract: Background Re-emerging infectious diseases continue to present major public health challenges in low-resource settings where surveillance systems often operate under significant infrastructural, financial and workforce constraints. Nigeria has experienced recurrent outbreaks of Lassa fever, cholera, yellow fever and mpox during the past decade, highlighting persistent weaknesses in disease detection, reporting and outbreak response. Digital surveillance systems have increasingly been introduced to strengthen epidemic preparedness and improve surveillance performance, yet evidence describing the contribution of Nigeria's two principal electronic surveillance platforms remains fragmented across disease-specific investigations and implementation studies. This paper synthesises the available evidence on the Surveillance Outbreak Response Management and Analysis System (SORMAS) and the electronic Integrated Disease Surveillance and Response (eIDSR) system, examining their contribution to strengthening infectious disease surveillance within Nigeria's public health system. Methods A focused narrative synthesis was undertaken to examine digital tools for managing re-emerging infectious diseases in Nigeria. The review followed established scoping review methodology and identified studies published between 2015 and 2026. Twenty-three eligible publications were included, from which evidence relating specifically to SORMAS and eIDSR was synthesised. Findings were organised around surveillance performance, reporting timeliness, data quality, outbreak detection and implementation experiences. Results The evidence consistently demonstrates that both surveillance systems have strengthened infectious disease surveillance in Nigeria. SORMAS has enhanced case-based surveillance through real-time reporting, electronic case management, laboratory integration and improved contact tracing. The eIDSR system has strengthened routine surveillance reporting, improved reporting completeness, accelerated notification of priority diseases and enhanced communication between peripheral health facilities and surveillance authorities. Despite these advances, implementation continues to be influenced by infrastructure limitations, workforce capacity and long-term sustainability. Conclusion SORMAS and eIDSR have become integral components of Nigeria's surveillance architecture and have substantially improved surveillance performance across several epidemic-prone diseases. Continued investment in infrastructure, interoperability, workforce development and surveillance governance will be essential to maximise their long-term contribution to epidemic preparedness and health system resilience.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 本综述探讨了数字监测系统在尼日利亚加强传染病监测中的作用,重点分析了SORMAS(疫情响应管理与分析系统)和电子综合疾病监测与响应(eIDSR)系统。核心问题关注这些系统如何在尼日利亚公共卫生系统中提升监测绩效、报告及时性、数据质量、疾病检测和实施经验。
