analysis_en.scope_and_question: The review examines the role of digital surveillance systems in strengthening infectious disease surveillance in Nigeria, focusing on the Surveillance Outbreak Response Management and Analysis System (SORMAS) and the electronic Integrated Disease Surveillance and Response (eIDSR) system. The central question addresses how these systems contribute to surveillance performance, reporting timeliness, data quality, outbreak detection, and implementation experiences within Nigeria's public health system.
analysis_en.evidence_base_and_review_method: A focused narrative synthesis was conducted following established scoping review methodology. Studies published between 2015 and 2026 were identified, and 23 eligible publications were included. Evidence specific to SORMAS and eIDSR was synthesized to assess their impact on surveillance performance.
analysis_en.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The evidence consistently demonstrates that both SORMAS and eIDSR have strengthened infectious disease surveillance in Nigeria. SORMAS enhanced case-based surveillance through real-time reporting, electronic case management, laboratory integration, and improved contact tracing. The eIDSR system strengthened routine surveillance reporting, improved reporting completeness, accelerated notification of priority diseases, and enhanced communication between peripheral health facilities and surveillance authorities.
analysis_en.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Implementation of these systems continues to be influenced by infrastructure limitations, workforce capacity, and long-term sustainability challenges. The review highlights persistent weaknesses in disease detection, reporting, and outbreak response despite advances in digital surveillance.
analysis_en.research_and_practice_implications: Continued investment in infrastructure, interoperability, workforce development, and surveillance governance is essential to maximize the long-term contribution of SORMAS and eIDSR to epidemic preparedness and health system resilience in Nigeria.

title_zh: 加强尼日利亚传染病监测:SORMAS和电子综合疾病监测与响应系统的重点范围综述
source_body_en: Background Re-emerging infectious diseases continue to present major public health challenges in low-resource settings where surveillance systems often operate under significant infrastructural, financial and workforce constraints. Nigeria has experienced recurrent outbreaks of Lassa fever, cholera, yellow fever and mpox during the past decade, highlighting persistent weaknesses in disease detection, reporting and outbreak response. Digital surveillance systems have increasingly been introduced to strengthen epidemic preparedness and improve surveillance performance, yet evidence describing the contribution of Nigeria's two principal electronic surveillance platforms remains fragmented across disease-specific investigations and implementation studies. This paper synthesises the available evidence on the Surveillance Outbreak Response Management and Analysis System (SORMAS) and the electronic Integrated Disease Surveillance and Response (eIDSR) system, examining their contribution to strengthening infectious disease surveillance within Nigeria's public health system. Methods A focused narrative synthesis was undertaken to examine digital tools for managing re-emerging infectious diseases in Nigeria. The review followed established scoping review methodology and identified studies published between 2015 and 2026. Twenty-three eligible publications were included, from which evidence relating specifically to SORMAS and eIDSR was synthesised. Findings were organised around surveillance performance, reporting timeliness, data quality, outbreak detection and implementation experiences. Results The evidence consistently demonstrates that both surveillance systems have strengthened infectious disease surveillance in Nigeria. SORMAS has enhanced case-based surveillance through real-time reporting, electronic case management, laboratory integration and improved contact tracing. The eIDSR system has strengthened routine surveillance reporting, improved reporting completeness, accelerated notification of priority diseases and enhanced communication between peripheral health facilities and surveillance authorities. Despite these advances, implementation continues to be influenced by infrastructure limitations, workforce capacity and long-term sustainability. Conclusion SORMAS and eIDSR have become integral components of Nigeria's surveillance architecture and have substantially improved surveillance performance across several epidemic-prone diseases. Continued investment in infrastructure, interoperability, workforce development and surveillance governance will be essential to maximise their long-term contribution to epidemic preparedness and health system resilience.
abstract_zh: 背景 再现性传染病继续在资源有限的环境中对公共卫生构成重大挑战,其中监测系统往往受到基础设施、资金和人力资源的显著限制。在过去十年中,尼日利亚经历了拉沙热、霍乱、黄热病等传染病的反复暴发,凸显了疾病监测、报告和响应方面的持续薄弱环节。数字监测系统越来越多地被引入以加强疫情准备并提高监测绩效,但描述尼日利亚两大主要电子监测平台贡献的证据仍然分散在针对特定疾病的研究和实施研究中。本文综合了关于SORMAS(疫情响应管理与分析系统)和电子综合疾病监测与响应(eIDSR)系统的现有证据,探讨它们在尼日利亚公共卫生系统中对加强传染病监测的贡献。方法 采用重点叙述综合方法,以评估数字工具在尼日利亚管理再现性传染病中的作用。综述遵循已建立的范围综述方法,确定了2015年至2026年间发表的研究。纳入了23项符合条件的出版物,从中综合了与SORMAS和eIDSR相关的具体证据。发现围绕监测绩效、报告及时性、数据质量、疾病检测和实施经验进行组织。结果 证据一致表明,这两个监测系统都增强了尼日利亚的传染病监测能力。SORMAS通过实时报告、电子病例管理、实验室整合和改进的接触追踪,提高了基于病例的监测能力。eIDSR系统加强了常规监测报告,提高了报告完整性,加快了优先疾病的通知,并增强了基层医疗机构与监测当局之间的沟通。尽管有这些进展,实施仍受到基础设施限制、人力资源能力和长期可持续性问题的影响。结论 SORMAS和eIDSR已成为尼日利亚监测架构的重要组成部分,并在多种疫情易发疾病中显著提高了监测绩效。继续投资于基础设施、互操作性、人力资源发展和监测治理对于最大化这些系统在疫情准备和卫生系统韧性的长期贡献至关重要。

title: High-Sensitivity Molecular Detection of Viral Bioaerosols Using a Composite Collection System and Optimized RPA–CRISPR/Cas12a
abstract: Abstract Highly pathogenic airborne microorganisms pose a significant public health threat, particularly because their small particle size can support prolonged suspension and long-range transport. Here, we present an integrated platform that combines a composite bioaerosol collection system with a three-stage enrichment mechanism and recombinase polymerase amplification–CRISPR/Cas12a (RPA–CRISPR/Cas12a) detection. The platform incorporates model-based constant-temperature control, stacked optical filters, and multichannel fluorescence imaging. The temperature-control model accurately described the thermal response of the reaction module, while the optical and imaging subsystems supported stable fluorescence readout. Using aerosolized monkeypox virus (MPXV) pseudovirus as a controlled test target, the platform detected target nucleic acid in collection liquid down to 10 copies/μL under the tested conditions. These results support the feasibility of integrating aerosol enrichment with isothermal molecular detection in a compact prototype. The main contributions lie in innovations and the engineering integration of bioaerosol collection and enrichment, thermal control of biochemical reactions in molecular detection, and precision fluorescence detection techniques for molecular detection. Regarding molecular detection methods, the biochemical reaction parameters were experimentally optimized rather than introducing new biochemical reaction mechanisms. Validation with authentic clinical or environmental viral aerosols remains necessary before diagnostic or field-use claims can be made.

abstract_original: Abstract Highly pathogenic airborne microorganisms pose a significant public health threat, particularly because their small particle size can support prolonged suspension and long-range transport. Here, we present an integrated platform that combines a composite bioaerosol collection system with a three-stage enrichment mechanism and recombinase polymerase amplification–CRISPR/Cas12a (RPA–CRISPR/Cas12a) detection. The platform incorporates model-based constant-temperature control, stacked optical filters, and multichannel fluorescence imaging. The temperature-control model accurately described the thermal response of the reaction module, while the optical and imaging subsystems supported stable fluorescence readout. Using aerosolized monkeypox virus (MPXV) pseudovirus as a controlled test target, the platform detected target nucleic acid in collection liquid down to 10 copies/μL under the tested conditions. These results support the feasibility of integrating aerosol enrichment with isothermal molecular detection in a compact prototype. The main contributions lie in innovations and the engineering integration of bioaerosol collection and enrichment, thermal control of biochemical reactions in molecular detection, and precision fluorescence detection techniques for molecular detection. Regarding molecular detection methods, the biochemical reaction parameters were experimentally optimized rather than introducing new biochemical reaction mechanisms. Validation with authentic clinical or environmental viral aerosols remains necessary before diagnostic or field-use claims can be made.
title_original: High-Sensitivity Molecular Detection of Viral Bioaerosols Using a Composite Collection System and Optimized RPA–CRISPR/Cas12a

abstract_zh: 摘要 高致病性气溶胶微生物对公共卫生构成显著威胁,尤其是其微小粒径可支持长时间悬浮并实现远距离传播。本研究提出了一种集成平台,该平台结合了复合生物气溶胶收集系统与三级富集机制,并采用重组酶聚合酶扩增–CRISPR/Cas12a(RPA–CRISPR/Cas12a)检测。该平台集成了基于模型的恒温控制、叠层光学滤光片及多通道荧光成像。温度控制模型准确描述了反应模块的热响应,而光学与成像子系统则支持稳定的荧光读出。使用气溶胶化猴痘病毒(MPXV)假病毒作为受控测试靶标,在测试条件下,该平台可检测到收集液中低至10拷贝/μL的靶标核酸。这些结果证明了在紧凑原型中集成气溶胶富集与等温分子检测的可行性。主要贡献在于生物气溶胶收集与富集、分子检测中生化反应的热控制以及分子检测精密荧光检测技术的创新与工程集成。在分子检测方法方面,生化反应参数通过实验优化而非引入新的生化反应机制。在做出诊断或现场使用声明前,仍需使用真实临床或环境病毒气溶胶进行验证。

title: Vigilância de zoonoses virais na Amazônia: saúde única, território e resposta a surtos
abstract: Vigilância de zoonoses virais na Amazônia apresenta uma abordagem integrada sobre os riscos, desafios e estratégias de vigilância de doenças virais em um dos territórios de maior biodiversidade do planeta. A obra discute a Amazônia como território sentinela, a abordagem de Saúde Única, os determinantes socioambientais, a vigilância humano–animal–ambiente, o diagnóstico em regiões remotas e a resposta às primeiras 72 horas de surtos. Também aborda aplicações práticas envolvendo febre Oropouche, COVID-19, Mpox e vírus Nipah. Destina-se a estudantes, pesquisadores e profissionais interessados em epidemiologia, saúde pública, zoonoses e vigilância em saúde.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addresses the need for integrated surveillance of viral zoonoses in the Amazon, focusing on the risks, challenges and strategies for monitoring viral diseases in a region of high biodiversity. The background highlights the importance of understanding the unique ecological and socioenvironmental factors that contribute to the emergence and spread of such diseases.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study is a book that discusses the Amazon as a sentinel territory, the One Health approach, socioenvironmental determinants, and the challenges of human–animal–environment surveillance. It also covers the diagnosis of diseases in remote regions and the response to the first 72 hours of outbreaks.
analysis.methods: The methods section outlines the practical applications of the study, including case studies on specific viruses such as febre Oropouche, COVID-19, Mpox and Nipah virus, which are used to illustrate the surveillance and response strategies discussed.
analysis.main_results: The main results include the identification of key factors influencing viral zoonoses in the Amazon, such as socioenvironmental determinants, and the discussion of surveillance and response strategies for diseases like Mpox.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret the findings as emphasizing the importance of integrating human, animal and environmental health in surveillance efforts, and they highlight the novelty of applying this approach to the unique context of the Amazon region.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform public health strategies for surveillance and rapid response to viral zoonoses in biodiverse regions, particularly in the context of diseases like Mpox.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is based on an abstract and does not provide detailed data or statistical analysis, which limits the confidence in its conclusions. The evidence is considered moderate due to the lack of specific numerical findings.

analysis.summary_en: This study explores the integrated surveillance of viral zoonoses in the Amazon, emphasizing the region's role as a sentinel territory for emerging diseases. It outlines the challenges of monitoring and responding to outbreaks in remote areas, focusing on the socioenvironmental determinants and the One Health approach. The book includes practical applications related to diseases such as Mpox, highlighting the importance of cross-sector collaboration. While the study provides a general framework for understanding viral zoonoses, its abstract-only nature limits the depth of its evidence. The findings suggest that a holistic approach is essential for effective disease surveillance and response, particularly in biodiverse regions. The study's implications for public health are significant, offering insights into the management of viral outbreaks in ecologically complex environments.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究探讨了亚马孙地区病毒性人兽共患病一体化监测的必要性,重点关注高生物多样性地区病毒性疾病的风险、挑战与监测策略。背景部分强调了理解独特生态与社会环境因素对疾病出现与传播的重要性。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究为一部著作,讨论了亚马孙作为哨点领土、一体化健康方法、社会环境决定因素以及人-动物-环境监测的挑战。同时涵盖了偏远地区疾病监测与暴发后首个72小时响应的内容。
elements_zh.methods: 方法部分概述了本研究的实践应用,包括针对特定病毒(如奥罗普切热、COVID-19、猴痘与尼帕病毒)的案例研究,用于阐释所讨论的监测与响应策略。
elements_zh.main_results: 主要结果包括识别影响亚马孙地区病毒性人兽共患病的关键因素(如社会环境决定因素),并讨论了猴痘等疾病的监测与响应策略。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将研究发现解释为强调在人兽共患病监测工作中整合人类、动物与环境健康的重要性,并突出了将该方法应用于亚马孙地区独特背景的创新性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果可为高生物多样性地区病毒性人兽共患病监测与快速响应提供公共卫生策略参考,特别是针对猴痘等疾病。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究基于摘要,未提供详细数据或统计分析,限制了结论的可信度。由于缺乏具体数值结果,证据强度被评估为中等。

full_text: Presentation Type: Poster Presentation Subject Category: Surveillance Abstract ID: 196 Breakthrough COVID-19 Infections Among Vaccinated Residents of VA Community Living Centers Brandon Smith1 EST Healthcare water management programs (WMPs) have historically emphasized the control of Legionella pneumophila, largely due to its estab- lished role in Legionnaires’ disease outbreaks. However, healthcare water systems harbor a wide range of opportunistic premise plumbing pathogens (OPPPs), including nontuberculous mycobacteria (NTM), Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Acinetobacter baumannii, Stenotrophomonas maltophilia, and Burkholderia cepacia complex. These organisms exhibit distinct eco- logical preferences and persistence mechanisms that vary by system type. In this study, we analyze microbiological testing data from more than 200,000 healthcare-associated water system samples collected since September 2019, comparing pathogen positivity across ice machines, gen- eral potable water, and cooling towers. Results demonstrate substantial variability in pathogen positivity by system type, with NTM showing mark- edly higher positivity in ice machines and potable water systems (relative to traditional indicator organisms). Legionella pneumophila positivity was highest in cooling towers but substantially lower in potable water. These findings indicate that uniform, organism-agnostic surveillance strategies are insufficient and that WMPs must be selectively designed based on sys- tem type, exposure route, and patient risk. Adopting site-specific, organ- ism-selective monitoring frameworks may significantly improve infection prevention efforts in healthcare settings. Antimicrobial Stewardship & Healthcare Epidemiology 2026;6(Suppl. S1):s185 doi:10.1017/ash.2026.10727 Presentation Type: Poster Presentation Subject Category: Surveillance Abstract ID: 226 Patterns and Gaps in Mpox Vaccination at NYC Health + Hospitals, a Large Urban Safety Net Health System in New York City, 2022-2025 Shatha AlShanqeeti1, Gaayathri Krishnan2, Crisanta Simon, Jonathan Baghdadi1, Katherine Goodman1, Gregory Schrank1, Jessica Holman, Lisa Pineles3, Cassie Cunningham Goedken4, Christine Firestone, KC Coffey5, Westyn Branch-Elliman, Surbhi Leekha6, Anthony Harris1 and Daniel Morgan1 1University of Maryland School of Medicine; 2University of Maryland; 3University of Maryland, Baltimore; 4Center for Access & Delivery Research & Evaluation (CADRE), Iowa City Veterans Affairs Health Care System, Iowa City, IA, USA; 5Massachusetts General Hospital and 6University of Maryland Baltimore Background: Hospital onset bacteremia and fungemia (HOB) is under development as a Center for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) auto- mated digital quality measure. We evaluated the use of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) in assessing attribution and preventability of HOB. Methods This is a retrospective cohort study of hospitalized patients with positive blood cultures at 11 US Veterans Affairs (VA) hospitals. We included a random sample of positive blood cultures collected after day 3 of admission where admission date is day 1. GenAI (OpenAI GPT- 4o) was prompted to provide the most likely source and adjudicate the pre- ventability of HOB using standardized prompts and clinical data (GenAI). IP experts used GenAI output to provide GenAI-assisted determinations of source and preventability of HOB (IP-AI). HOB event preventability was rated by IP expert using a 6-point Likert scale, responses were combined to 3 categories for analysis. We compared initial GenAI with IP-AI determi- nations of source and preventability. A separate human-only review by a different IP expert was performed (IP-alone) on a random subset to com- pare time required for review. Results We included 52 HOB events for IP- AI and a subset of 21 for IP-alone. Enterobacterales were the most common organisms (22/52, 42%) followed by Staphylococcus aureus (9/52, 17%). Median duration to HOB event was 12 (IQR 5 – 31) days. GenAI most commonly attributed bacteremia to gastrointestinal (GI) (14/52, 26.9%), followed by genitourinary (GU) (12/52, 23%), central line (CLABSI) (8/ 52, 15%), and skin and soft tissue infections (SSTI) (7/52, 14%) sources (Figure 1). IP-AI determination of source agreed with GenAI source in 67% (35/52) of cases. Most agreement between IP-AI and GenAI occurred when HOB was attributed to a bone and joint infection (2/2, 100%), fol- lowed by GI source (13/14, 93%), SSTI (5/7, 71%), and GU source (7/12, 58%). Most disagreements (17/52, 33%) occurred when IP-AI attribution was to an unknown source (5/17, 29%) or blood culture contamination (3/ 17, 18%). GenAI adjudication of preventability matched IP-AI adjudica- tion in 20/52 (39%). The median time to complete an IP-AI review was 11.5 (IQR 6 – 20.5) minutes compared to a median of 25 (IQR 13 – 33) minutes for IP-alone. Conclusion IP experts often agreed with GenAI for source of HOB but disagreed with its preventability. GenAI rarely acknowledged unknown source. Using GenAI for HOB detection is faster than human review but must account for differences in preventability. Antimicrobial Stewardship & Healthcare Epidemiology 2026;6(Suppl. analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to evaluate the use of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) in assessing the attribution and preventability of hospital-onset bacteremia and fungemia (HOB) events.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This is a retrospective cohort study of hospitalized patients with positive blood cultures at 11 US Veterans Affairs (VA) hospitals, including a random sample of positive blood cultures collected after day 3 of admission.
analysis.methods: GenAI (OpenAI GPT-4o) was prompted to provide the most likely source and adjudicate the preventability of HOB using standardized prompts and clinical data. IP experts used GenAI output to provide GenAI-assisted determinations of source and preventability, and a separate human-only review by a different IP expert was performed on a random subset.
analysis.main_results: GenAI most commonly attributed bacteremia to gastrointestinal (GI) sources (14/52, 26.9%), followed by genitourinary (GU) (12/52, 23%), central line (CLABSI) (8/52, 15%), and skin and soft tissue infections (SSTI) (7/52, 14%) sources. IP-AI determination of source agreed with GenAI source in 67% (35/52) of cases, while GenAI adjudication of preventability matched IP-AI adjudication in 20/52 (39%).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors concluded that IP experts often agreed with GenAI for the source of HOB but disagreed with its preventability, indicating that while GenAI can assist in identifying sources, it may not be reliable for assessing preventability.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings suggest that integrating GenAI into HOB surveillance could enhance the speed of source identification but must be complemented by expert judgment for preventability assessments, which is critical for infection prevention strategies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on GenAI for preventability adjudication, which may not align with expert opinions, and the small sample size of HOB events analyzed. The evidence is moderate due to these limitations.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the use of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) in assessing the attribution and preventability of hospital-onset bacteremia and fungemia (HOB) events. A retrospective cohort study was conducted on hospitalized patients with positive blood cultures at 11 US Veterans Affairs (VA) hospitals, focusing on HOB events occurring after day 3 of admission. GenAI was used to identify potential sources of HOB, and IP experts provided GenAI-assisted determinations. The results showed that GenAI attributed HOB events to gastrointestinal sources most frequently, with IP-AI agreeing with GenAI in 67% of cases. However, GenAI's preventability assessments matched IP-AI only in 39% of cases. The study highlights that while GenAI can expedite source identification, its role in preventability assessments requires expert validation. The findings suggest that integrating GenAI into HOB surveillance could improve efficiency but must be paired with human expertise for accurate preventability judgments. The evidence is moderate due to the limitations in GenAI's preventability adjudication and the relatively small sample size.

Results demonstrate substantial variability in pathogen positivity by system type, with NTM showing mark- edly higher positivity in ice machines and potable water systems (relative to traditional indicator organisms). These findings indicate that uniform, organism-agnostic surveillance strategies are insufficient and that WMPs must be selectively designed based on sys- tem type, exposure route, and patient risk. Methods This is a retrospective cohort study of hospitalized patients with positive blood cultures at 11 US Veterans Affairs (VA) hospitals. A separate human-only review by a different IP expert was performed (IP-alone) on a random subset to com- pare time required for review. Results We included 52 HOB events for IP- AI and a subset of 21 for IP-alone. The median time to complete an IP-AI review was 11.5 (IQR 6 – 20.5) minutes compared to a median of 25 (IQR 13 – 33) minutes for IP-alone. Conclusion IP experts often agreed with GenAI for source of HOB but disagreed with its preventability. analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在评估生成式人工智能(GenAI)在评估医院相关菌血症和真菌血症(HOB)事件的归因及可预防性方面的应用价值。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究为一项回顾性 队列研究 研究,纳入了美国11家退伍军人事务管理局(VA)医院中血培养阳性的住院患者,并随机纳入了住院第3天之后采集的阳性血培养样本。
analysis_zh.methods: GenAI(OpenAI GPT-4o)被提示使用标准化提示及临床数据,提供最可能的感染来源并判定 HOB 的可预防性。感染预防专家基于 GenAI 输出结果提供 GenAI 辅助的感染来源及可预防性判定,另一名感染预防专家对随机子集进行了单独人工审查。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者得出结论:感染预防专家在 HOB 感染来源判定上常与 GenAI 一致,但在可预防性评估上存在分歧,这表明 GenAI 可协助识别感染来源,但在可预防性评估方面可能不可靠。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,将 GenAI 集成至 HOB 感染预防工作中,可提高感染来源识别速度,但必须结合专家判断进行可预防性评估,这对感染预防策略至关重要。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究受限于对可预防性判定依赖 GenAI,其结果可能与专家意见不一致,且分析的 HOB 事件样本量较小。由于上述局限性,证据强度为中等。

Inaccurate allergy labels contribute to increased healthcare costs, SHEA Spring 2026 Abstracts S44 2026;6 Suppl 1 Clostridioides difficile infection, and suboptimal or unnecessary antibiotic use. We aimed to characterize the incidence and features of inpatient anti- biotic-associated allergic reactions, including serious events, and to deter- mine the proportion of antibiotic regimens that were inappropriately modified in response to reported allergies. Methods: We conducted a retrospective study of patients ≤18 years admitted to Severance Children’s Hospital (Republic of Korea) during 2022–2024 who received oral or intravenous antibacterials and had an antibiotic-related adverse drug reaction (ADR) documented as “allergy” in the electronic health rec- ord. ADRs to antiviral, antifungal, or antiparasitic agents and reactions occurring in outpatient or emergency settings were excluded. Each discrete sign or symptom attributed to an antibiotic was counted as one allergic- reaction event. Management was considered appropriate if first-line therapy was continued for mild reactions, discontinued when unnecessary, aligned with international or national guidelines, or reflected pediatric infectious diseases expert opinion. Results: Among 31,164 admissions, 17,614 (56.0%) patients received antibiotics. A total of 215 antibiotic- related ADRs (0.92%) were documented, including 161 allergic-reaction events in 122 patients (0.7%) associated with 143 antibiotic prescriptions. Males accounted for 59.0% of cases; median age was 7.8 years (IQR, 2.8– 12.4). The most common indications were surgical prophylaxis (34.3%), systemic febrile illness (14.0%), and pneumonia (11.2%). Frequent mani- festations included nausea/vomiting (32.3%), urticaria (23.6%), and non- urticarial rash (18.1%). ?-lactams accounted for 67.3% of implicated agents; the most frequent drugs were ceftriaxone (26.8%), vancomycin (15.7%), and ampicillin/sulbactam (5.9%). Anaphylaxis occurred in 6 patients (5.0% of reactions; 0.002% of antibiotic prescriptions). Overall, 28.7% of allergy-labeled reactions were managed inappropriately, and 8.4% resulted in unnecessary escalation to broader-spectrum antibiotics (Table 1). Surgical prophylaxis was associated with reduced odds of inappropriate management compared with therapeutic use (OR, 0.46; 95% CI, 0.22– 0.99; P Conclusion: True antibiotic allergy in hospitalized children is uncommon, yet nearly one third of reported allergies led to suboptimal or inappropriate antibiotic use. Determining a Goal Central Line Standardized Utilization Ratio Necessary to Decrease Infections Shinya Hasegawa1 and Hiroyuki Suzuki2 1University of Iowa Health Care and 2University of Iowa Background: Diverticulitis is a common cause of emergency department (ED) visits for abdominal pain. Although recent guidelines recommend selective antibiotic use for low-risk cases, antibiotics remain commonly prescribed. Facility-level variation in prescribing practices has been under- reported. Methods: We conducted a retrospective cohort study (2016– 2023) using the Veterans Health Administration (VHA) Corporate Data Warehouse. We identified ED visits for a first episode of diverticulitis and excluded patients admitted within 48 hours. Low-risk cases were defined using International Classification Disease-10 codes for diverticu- litis without perforation or abscess, Charlson Comorbidity Index <2, white blood cell (WBC) count <15 x 10^3 /?L, and C-reactive protein <14 mg/dL. We applied a multivariable mixed-effects logistic regression model with random facility intercepts to assess variation in antibiotic prescribing across VHA facilities, adjusting for patient demographics, WBC count, and facility complexity level. Adjusted odds ratios (ORs) and 95% confi- dence intervals (CIs) were estimated to assess the associations between patient-level variables and antibiotic prescription. Facility-level variation was quantified using the median odds ratio (MOR). Bootstrap resampling (2,000 iterations) was used to estimate 95% CIs for the MOR. Result: Among 4,214 patients (median age, 51 years; 84.6% male) from 72 facilities with ?10 eligible encounters, 176 (4.2%) did not receive antibiotics and 4,038 (95.8%) received antibiotics at ED discharge. Compared with patients who received antibiotics, those not receiving antibioitcs were less often White (72.1% vs. 76.7%). Abnormal WBC count was associated with antibiotic prescribing in the multivariable logistic regression model (adjusted OR 2.15 [95% CI: 1.13-4.08], p=0.019; Table). Facility-specific adjusted ORs ranged from 0.26 (95% CI: 0.14-0.48) to 1.50 (95% CI: 0.60-3.79), indicating heterogeneity in prescribing practices across the VHA system (Figure). The MOR for the facility-level variation in antibiotic prescribing was 1.70 (95% bootstrap CI: 1.00-2.22), suggesting a median 70% difference in the odds of receiving antibiotics between two otherwise identical patients treated at randomly selected facilities. In one significantly low-prescribing facility, review of 63 providers caring for 83 patients showed that among 13 providers who saw low-risk diverticulitis on more than three occasions, 10 prescribed antibiotics in all encounters, 2 in 50- 99% of encounters, and 1 in 33%, suggesting provider-level variation. Conclusion: In this nationwide VHA cohort of low-risk diverticulitis, anti- biotic prescribing varied across facilities after accounting for patient char- acteristics and facility complexity. The MOR indicates significant facility- level variation in antibiotic prescribing across facilities, highlighting oppor- tunities for targeted antibiotic stewardship and implementation strategies to improve guideline-concordant care. S1):s46 doi:10.1017/ash.2026.10492 Presentation Type: Poster Presentation Subject Category: Antibiotic Stewardship Abstract ID: 62 National Data Indicates Increases in the Burden of Clostridioides dif- ficile infections in the United States Following COVID-19 Pandemic Ayesha Samreen1, Omar Abu Saleh and Lynn Estes2 1Mayo Clinic, Infectious diseases and 2Mayo Clinic Background: Ceftriaxone and cefepime resistance among Enterobacterales continues to increase globally, partly due to the rising prevalence of extended-spectrum β-lactamase (ESBL) producing organisms. Surveillance of both resistance patterns and antimicrobial utilization is essential to inform empiric prescribing practices and stewardship strate- gies. Determining a Goal Central Line Standardized Utilization Ratio Necessary to Decrease Infections Shinya Hasegawa1 and Hiroyuki Suzuki2 1University of Iowa Health Care and 2University of Iowa Background: Diverticulitis is a common cause of emergency department (ED) visits for abdominal pain. Although recent guidelines recommend selective antibiotic use for low-risk cases, antibiotics remain commonly prescribed. Facility-level variation in prescribing practices has been under- reported. Methods: We conducted a retrospective cohort study (2016– 2023) using the Veterans Health Administration (VHA) Corporate Data Warehouse. We identified ED visits for a first episode of diverticulitis and excluded patients admitted within 48 hours. Low-risk cases were defined using International Classification Disease-10 codes for diverticu- litis without perforation or abscess, Charlson Comorbidity Index <2, white blood cell (WBC) count <15 x 10^3 /?L, and C-reactive protein <14 mg/dL. We applied a multivariable mixed-effects logistic regression model with random facility intercepts to assess variation in antibiotic prescribing across VHA facilities, adjusting for patient demographics, WBC count, and facility complexity level. Adjusted odds ratios (ORs) and 95% confi- dence intervals (CIs) were estimated to assess the associations between patient-level variables and antibiotic prescription. Facility-level variation was quantified using the median odds ratio (MOR). Bootstrap resampling (2,000 iterations) was used to estimate 95% CIs for the MOR. Result: Among 4,214 patients (median age, 51 years; 84.6% male) from 72 facilities with ?10 eligible encounters, 176 (4.2%) did not receive antibiotics and 4,038 (95.8%) received antibiotics at ED discharge. Abnormal WBC count was associated with antibiotic prescribing in the multivariable logistic regression model (adjusted OR 2.15 [95% CI: 1.13-4.08], p=0.019; Table). Facility-specific adjusted ORs ranged from 0.26 (95% CI: 0.14-0.48) to 1.50 (95% CI: 0.60-3.79), indicating heterogeneity in prescribing practices across the VHA system (Figure). The MOR for the facility-level variation in antibiotic prescribing was 1.70 (95% bootstrap CI: 1.00-2.22), suggesting a median 70% difference in the odds of receiving antibiotics between two otherwise identical patients treated at randomly selected facilities. In one significantly low-prescribing facility, review of 63 providers caring for 83 patients showed that among 13 providers who saw low-risk diverticulitis on more than three occasions, 10 prescribed antibiotics in all encounters, 2 in 50- 99% of encounters, and 1 in 33%, suggesting provider-level variation. Conclusion: In this nationwide VHA cohort of low-risk diverticulitis, anti- biotic prescribing varied across facilities after accounting for patient char- acteristics and facility complexity. The MOR indicates significant facility- level variation in antibiotic prescribing across facilities, highlighting oppor- tunities for targeted antibiotic stewardship and implementation strategies to improve guideline-concordant care. S1):s42–s43 doi:10.1017/ash.2026.10489 Presentation Type: Oral Presentation Subject Category: Vaccination Abstract ID: 59 Clear After a Year? Insights from a Pediatric Approach to Contact Precaution Discontinuation for Resistant Gram-Negatives Organisms Anthony Lo Piccolo1, Emma Kaplan-Lewis2, Kruti Gala3, Eunice Casey3, Gabriel Cohen4, Stephanie Rasmussen5, Andrew Wallach4, Ofole Mgbako5 and Justin Chan5 1NYU Langone Health; 2NYC Health and Hospitals; 3NYC Health + Hospitals; 4NYC Health + Hospitals/Bellevue and 5NYU Grossman School of Medicine Background: NYC Health + Hospitals (H+H) provides care to large com- munities experiencing social vulnerability. During the 2022 mpox out- break, H+H implemented a large-scale, targeted mpox vaccination campaign using electronic health record (EHR) reminders among groups with greatest risk of mpox infection. When demand was high, 25% of avail- able vaccine appointments were reserved for established H+H patients. This study aims to describe patterns of mpox vaccination amongst eligible H+H patient groups. Methods: H+H started vaccinating with JYNNEOS in May 2022 and used EHR reminders to encourage vaccination amongst those eligible, including: (1) Patients with an HIV diagnosis AND who had a sexually transmitted infection in the past year; OR (2) Patients who received at least one mpox vaccine and was due for the second; OR (3) Patients with a sexual orientation in the EHR as Gay, Bisexual, Lesbian, Something else, or Choose not to disclose; OR (4) Patients with a gender identity in the EHR as Transgender Female, Transgender Male, Gender Non-binary/Nonconforming, Other, or Choose not to disclose. We extracted data from the NYC Citywide Immunization Registry through April 30, 2025, into our EHR. We calculated a Pearson correlation coeffi- cient between the 2022 Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) Social Vulnerability Index (SVI) and percentage who received at least one mpox vaccination by zip code with significance set at a p-value <0.05. Results: Figure 1 summarizes key events along the H+H mpox vaccination timeline. There were 112,680 H+H patients eligible for mpox vaccination, of which 25.7% received at least one dose by April 2025, compared to 51.5% amongst patients with HIV (Table). White patients had the highest SHEA Spring 2026 Abstracts 2026;6 Suppl 1 S43 proportion vaccinated (31.1%), and Hispanic/Latinx patients had the low- est (22.0%). Figure 2 indicates the percentage vaccinated by neighborhood at three time points (September 2022, April 2023, April 2025). As of April 2025, the percentage of eligible individuals vaccinated by zip code was neg- atively correlated with SVI of the zip code (r= -0.0529; p<0.01) (Figure 3). Conclusion: Amongst eligible H+H patients, we identified disparities in mpox vaccination rates by race/ethnicity, neighborhood, and the zip code SVI. The use of EHR reminders may have helped us achieve a higher vac- cination rate amongst eligible patients with HIV, compared to the overall cohort. A limitation may be misclassification of eligible individuals, which relies on structured social history and gender identity data accurately doc- umented in the EHR. Our findings identify areas for quality improvement to optimize vaccine equity. Antimicrobial Stewardship & Healthcare Epidemiology 2026;6(Suppl. analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to describe patterns of mpox vaccination amongst eligible H+H patient groups, highlighting disparities in vaccination rates by race/ethnicity, neighborhood, and the zip code Social Vulnerability Index (SVI).
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study was conducted by NYC Health + Hospitals (H+H) from May 2022 to April 2025, focusing on 112,680 eligible H+H patients, including those with HIV, those due for a second mpox vaccine, and those with specific sexual orientations or gender identities.
analysis.methods: H+H used electronic health record (EHR) reminders to encourage vaccination among eligible patients, and data were extracted from the NYC Citywide Immunization Registry. A Pearson correlation coefficient was calculated between the 2022 CDC Social Vulnerability Index (SVI) and vaccination rates by zip code.
analysis.main_results: As of April 2025, 25.7% of eligible H+H patients received at least one mpox dose, with 51.5% of patients with HIV vaccinated. White patients had the highest vaccination proportion (31.1%), and Hispanic/Latinx patients had the lowest (22.0%). Vaccination rates were negatively correlated with SVI (r= -0.0529; p<0.01).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted these findings as evidence of disparities in mpox vaccination rates by race/ethnicity, neighborhood, and SVI, identifying areas for quality improvement to optimize vaccine equity.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings can inform strategies to improve vaccine equity and address disparities in mpox vaccination rates, particularly in resource-limited settings with high social vulnerability.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: A limitation may be misclassification of eligible individuals, which relies on structured social history and gender identity data accurately documented in the EHR. The evidence is moderate, as it is based on observational data and correlation analysis.

analysis.summary_en: This study examines mpox vaccination patterns among eligible patients at NYC Health + Hospitals (H+H) from May 2022 to April 2025. It highlights disparities in vaccination rates by race/ethnicity, neighborhood, and the Social Vulnerability Index (SVI) of zip codes. The authors found that 25.7% of eligible H+H patients received at least one mpox dose by April 2025, with higher rates among patients with HIV. White patients had the highest vaccination proportion (31.1%), while Hispanic/Latinx patients had the lowest (22.0%). Vaccination rates were negatively correlated with SVI (r= -0.0529; p<0.01). The study suggests that EHR reminders may have contributed to higher vaccination rates among certain groups. The authors note limitations related to potential misclassification of eligible individuals and emphasize the need for quality improvement to enhance vaccine equity. These findings have implications for public health strategies, particularly in addressing disparities in vaccination access and outcomes.

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究由纽约市卫生+医院(H+H)于2022年5月至2025年4月开展,涵盖112,680名符合条件的H+H患者,包括HIV感染者、需接种第二剂猴痘疫苗的患者,以及具有特定性取向或性别认同的患者。
elements_zh.methods: H+H通过电子健康记录(EHR)提醒鼓励符合条件患者接种疫苗,并从纽约市全市免疫登记系统提取数据。研究计算了2022年CDC社会脆弱性指数(SVI)与各邮政编码猴痘疫苗接种率之间的皮尔逊相关系数。
elements_zh.main_results: 截至2025年4月,25.7%的符合条件H+H患者至少接种了一剂猴痘疫苗,其中HIV感染者的接种率为51.5%。白人患者的猴痘疫苗接种比例最高(31.1%),而西班牙裔/拉丁裔患者最低(22.0%)。猴痘疫苗接种率与SVI呈负相关(r= -0.0529;p<0.01)。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将这些发现解释为猴痘疫苗接种率在种族/民族、社区及SVI方面存在差异的证据,并指出需通过质量改进措施优化猴痘疫苗接种公平性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可为改善猴痘疫苗接种公平性及解决不同SVI地区猴痘疫苗接种率差异的策略提供参考,特别是在资源有限且社会脆弱性高的环境中。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 研究可能存在对符合条件个体的误分类,该分类依赖于EHR中结构化社会史与性别认同数据的准确记录。证据强度为中等,因其基于观察性数据与相关性分析。

analysis_en.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to describe patterns of mpox vaccination amongst eligible H+H patient groups, highlighting disparities in vaccination rates by race/ethnicity, neighborhood, and the zip code Social Vulnerability Index (SVI).
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: The study was conducted by NYC Health + Hospitals (H+H) from May 2022 to April 2025, focusing on 112,680 eligible H+H patients, including those with HIV, those due for a second mpox vaccine, and those with specific sexual orientations or gender identities.
analysis_en.methods: H+H used electronic health record (EHR) reminders to encourage vaccination among eligible patients, and data were extracted from the NYC Citywide Immunization Registry. A Pearson correlation coefficient was calculated between the 2022 CDC Social Vulnerability Index (SVI) and vaccination rates by zip code.
analysis_en.main_results: As of April 2025, 25.7% of eligible H+H patients received at least one mpox dose, with 51.5% of patients with HIV vaccinated. White patients had the highest vaccination proportion (31.1%), and Hispanic/Latinx patients had the lowest (22.0%). Vaccination rates were negatively correlated with SVI (r= -0.0529; p<0.01).
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted these findings as evidence of disparities in mpox vaccination rates by race/ethnicity, neighborhood, and SVI, identifying areas for quality improvement to optimize vaccine equity.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings can inform strategies to improve vaccine equity and address disparities in mpox vaccination rates, particularly in resource-limited settings with high social vulnerability.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: A limitation may be misclassification of eligible individuals, which relies on structured social history and gender identity data accurately documented in the EHR. The evidence is moderate, as it is based on observational data and correlation analysis.

full_text: Presentation Type: Oral Presentation Subject Category: Surveillance Abstract ID: 54 From Benchmark to Best Practice: Reducing Blood Culture Contamination in Sepsis Care Brad Krier1, Jean Barth2 and W. Charles Huskins2 1Mayo Clinic Health System- Mankato and 2Mayo Clinic Background: A measles case requires immediate action to identify and administer prophylaxis to exposed individuals in healthcare settings. Infection preventionists (IPs) often balance proactive contact tracing with waiting for a positive test result. Objective: To develop a tool that enables IPs to stratify suspect measles cases by risk level, thereby supporting the decision to prioritize or defer active intervention while awaiting test results. Methods: In spring 2025, we developed a preliminary matrix and used 19 additional suspect patients to further refine the scoring of the tool. In August 2025, we deployed a finalized tool. The two-dimensional risk matrix incorporated both epidemiological risk factors and clinical risk fac- tors, each scored numerically based on yes or no questions. The sum of both categories was used to assign a final risk level that determined the rec- ommendations for IPs (Figure 1). The study population included patients tested for measles during the implementation period. Descriptive statistics were used to summarize the distribution of risk categories and outcomes. Among the whole cohort, Firth’s logistic regression was used to evaluate the association between clinical or epidemiological risk score and measles diagnosis. Among the production cohort, sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value (PPV) and negative predictive value (NPV) were calcu- lated to evaluate the diagnostic performance. Results: Since implementa- tion, the matrix was applied to 56 patients tested for measles. Of these, 10.7% (n=6) were categorized as high risk, 32.1% (n=18) as medium, and 57.1% (n=32) as low. Four of the 56 patients were positive for measles, 3 were categorized as high-risk and 1 as medium risk. Each one-unit increase in epidemiological risk was associated with a 2 folds increase in the odds of a positive measles diagnosis (odds ratio = 2.0; 95% CI, 1.3– 3.6). The low-risk category had an NPV of 1, indicating that all low?risk patients tested negative, thus supporting safe workload reduction by deprioritizing these cases. Conclusion: The Measles Exposure Response Risk Matrix effectively stratified cases and supported IP prioritization efforts. Low-risk groups required no action, expedited testing was reason- able for medium-risk cases, and proactive actions were reserved for high- risk cases. Clinical and epidemiologic risk scores progressed from arbitrary assignment to validated metrics, confirmed by statistical analysis. The flex- ible design permits adaptation to other infectious diseases, including avian influenza and mpox. With rising measles incidence, tools like this matrix will be essential to support rapid, evidence-based actions by infection pre- vention teams. Erika Paola Viana Cardenas1 1Stanford University Background: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is a growing global health threat, yet surveillance systems remain heavily centered on clinical report- ing and often overlook environmental transmission pathways. Urban riv- ers receiving mixed municipal, hospital, and agricultural inputs may act as important reservoirs and dissemination routes for antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs), particularly in resource-limited settings. Understanding spatial patterns of environmental resistomes is essential for advancing One Health–informed AMR surveillance. Methods: We conducted a longi- tudinal, multi-site investigation of ARG occurrence along the Cuautla River, an urban watershed in Morelos, Mexico, serving the resource-lim- ited city of Cuautla. Surface water samples were collected across six loca- tions spanning urban upstream (L1-2), urban core (L3-5), and urban downstream zones (L6) (Figure 1). Targeted droplet digital PCR (ddPCR) was used to quantify relevant ARGs, including Gram-positives (mecA and vanA), Gram-negatives beta-lactamases (CTX-M and SHV), AmpC-type β-lactamase (CMY), and Carbapenemase (KPC, NDM, VIM, IMP, and OXA-48), tetracycline (tetW) and Polymyxin-resistant (MCR-1). Physicochemical parameters and fecal indicator bacteria were measured concurrently to contextualize microbial contamination. Spatial and temporal trends in ARG abundance and composition were evaluated using non-parametric statistical analyses. Results: ARGs were widely detected across the watershed, with particularly high abundances of tetW, CMY, TEM, and multiple Gram-negative carbapenemase genes, including KPC, OXA-48, and VIM. The plasmid-mediated colistin resis- tance gene mcr-1 was also detected at multiple sites, highlighting the envi- ronmental presence of resistance determinants associated with last-resort antimicrobials (Figure 2). ARG abundances generally increased from urban upstream to urban downstream locations, likely reflecting cumula- tive inputs from domestic wastewater, healthcare facilities, and densely populated areas. Although ARG loads peaked within the urban core, elevated resistance signals remained detectable in downstream urban edge regions (Figure 3). In contrast to largely compliant physicochemical con- ditions, fecal indicator bacteria revealed pervasive microbial contamina- tion across urban sites. Conclusions: Our findings demonstrate extensive resistome contamination within an urban river system, encom- passing both environmental and clinically important ARGs. The spatial accumulation of resistance signals downstream and the detection of coli- stin resistance genes underscore the role of river ecosystem as conduits linking human activity to broader environmental AMR dissemination. SHEA Spring 2026 Abstracts S42 2026;6 Suppl 1 These results highlight the need to integrate environmental water surveil- lance into AMR monitoring frameworks and support a One Health approach that connects wastewater management, antibiotic stewardship, and public-health protection in resource-limited settings. Results: Figure 1 summarizes key events along the H+H mpox vaccination timeline. elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在开发一款工具,供感染预防团队按风险等级对疑似麻疹病例进行分层,从而在等待检测结果期间支持决定优先或延迟主动干预。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 研究人群包括在实施期间接受麻疹检测的患者,并通过19名额外疑似患者进一步完善风险矩阵。
elements_zh.methods: 研究构建了一份二维风险矩阵,整合流行病学和临床风险因素,每个因素基于“是”或“否”问题进行数值评分。两类评分之和用于分配最终风险等级。采用描述性统计总结风险类别和结局的分布,并使用Firth logistic回归评估临床或流行病学风险评分与麻疹诊断的关联。
elements_zh.main_results: 该矩阵应用于56名麻疹检测患者,其中10.7%(n=6)被归类为高风险,32.1%(n=18)为中等风险,57.1%(n=32)为低风险。在56名患者中,有4名麻疹检测结果为阳性,其中3名被归类为高风险,1名为中等风险。流行病学风险每增加一个单位,麻疹诊断阳性的几率增加2倍(优势比=2.0;95%置信区间,1.3–3.6)。低风险类别的阴性预测值为1,表明所有低风险患者检测结果均为阴性。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果支持使用该风险矩阵指导感染预防团队基于风险等级优先采取行动,该工具通过统计分析验证,并在不同风险类别中展现出实际应用价值。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 该工具可为感染预防团队提供快速、循证的行动依据,尤其在麻疹病例管理和降低低风险人群不必要检测方面具有指导意义。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究受限于单一队列研究的依赖,以及风险分类可能存在的偏倚。证据强度为中等,因该工具虽通过统计分析验证,但未在更广泛人群中测试。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在开发一款工具,供感染预防团队按风险等级对疑似麻疹病例进行分层,从而在等待检测结果期间支持决定优先或延迟主动干预。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 研究人群包括在实施期间接受麻疹检测的患者,并通过19名额外疑似患者进一步完善风险矩阵。
analysis_zh.methods: 研究构建了一份二维风险矩阵,整合流行病学和临床风险因素,每个因素基于“是”或“否”问题进行数值评分。两类评分之和用于分配最终风险等级。采用描述性统计总结风险类别和结局的分布,并使用Firth logistic回归评估临床或流行病学风险评分与麻疹诊断的关联。
analysis_zh.main_results: 该矩阵应用于56名麻疹检测患者,其中10.7%(n=6)被归类为高风险,32.1%(n=18)为中等风险,57.1%(n=32)为低风险。在56名患者中,有4名麻疹检测结果为阳性,其中3名被归类为高风险,1名为中等风险。流行病学风险每增加一个单位,麻疹诊断阳性的几率增加2倍(优势比=2.0;95%置信区间,1.3–3.6)。低风险类别的阴性预测值为1,表明所有低风险患者检测结果均为阴性。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果支持使用该风险矩阵指导感染预防团队基于风险等级优先采取行动,该工具通过统计分析验证,并在不同风险类别中展现出实际应用价值。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 该工具可为感染预防团队提供快速、循证的行动依据,尤其在麻疹病例管理和降低低风险人群不必要检测方面具有指导意义。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究受限于单一队列研究的依赖,以及风险分类可能存在的偏倚。证据强度为中等,因该工具虽通过统计分析验证,但未在更广泛人群中测试。

full_text: Presentation Type: Oral Presentation Subject Category: Surveillance Abstract ID: 54 From Benchmark to Best Practice: Reducing Blood Culture Contamination in Sepsis Care Brad Krier1, Jean Barth2 and W. Charles Huskins2 1Mayo Clinic Health System- Mankato and 2Mayo Clinic Background: A measles case requires immediate action to identify and administer prophylaxis to exposed individuals in healthcare settings. Infection preventionists (IPs) often balance proactive contact tracing with waiting for a positive test result. Objective: To develop a tool that enables IPs to stratify suspect measles cases by risk level, thereby supporting the decision to prioritize or defer active intervention while awaiting test results. Methods: In spring 2025, we developed a preliminary matrix and used 19 additional suspect patients to further refine the scoring of the tool. In August 2025, we deployed a finalized tool. The two-dimensional risk matrix incorporated both epidemiological risk factors and clinical risk fac- tors, each scored numerically based on yes or no questions. The sum of both categories was used to assign a final risk level that determined the rec- ommendations for IPs (Figure 1). The study population included patients tested for measles during the implementation period. Descriptive statistics were used to summarize the distribution of risk categories and outcomes. Among the whole cohort, Firth’s logistic regression was used to evaluate the association between clinical or epidemiological risk score and measles diagnosis. Among the production cohort, sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value (PPV) and negative predictive value (NPV) were calcu- lated to evaluate the diagnostic performance. Results: Since implementa- tion, the matrix was applied to 56 patients tested for measles. Of these, 10.7% (n=6) were categorized as high risk, 32.1% (n=18) as medium, and 57.1% (n=32) as low. Four of the 56 patients were positive for measles, 3 were categorized as high-risk and 1 as medium risk. Each one-unit increase in epidemiological risk was associated with a 2 folds increase in the odds of a positive measles diagnosis (odds ratio = 2.0; 95% CI, 1.3– 3.6). The low-risk category had an NPV of 1, indicating that all low?risk patients tested negative, thus supporting safe workload reduction by deprioritizing these cases. Conclusion: The Measles Exposure Response Risk Matrix effectively stratified cases and supported IP prioritization efforts. Low-risk groups required no action, expedited testing was reason- able for medium-risk cases, and proactive actions were reserved for high- risk cases. Clinical and epidemiologic risk scores progressed from arbitrary assignment to validated metrics, confirmed by statistical analysis. The flex- ible design permits adaptation to other infectious diseases, including avian influenza and mpox. With rising measles incidence, tools like this matrix will be essential to support rapid, evidence-based actions by infection pre- vention teams. S1):s42 doi:10.1017/ash.2026.10488 Presentation Type: Oral Presentation Subject Category: Surveillance Abstract ID: 56 The Prevalence of Uropathogens and Antimicrobial Susceptibility Profiles Encountered in Western India. Erika Paola Viana Cardenas1 1Stanford University Background: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is a growing global health threat, yet surveillance systems remain heavily centered on clinical report- ing and often overlook environmental transmission pathways. Urban riv- ers receiving mixed municipal, hospital, and agricultural inputs may act as important reservoirs and dissemination routes for antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs), particularly in resource-limited settings. Understanding spatial patterns of environmental resistomes is essential for advancing One Health–informed AMR surveillance. Methods: We conducted a longi- tudinal, multi-site investigation of ARG occurrence along the Cuautla River, an urban watershed in Morelos, Mexico, serving the resource-lim- ited city of Cuautla. Surface water samples were collected across six loca- tions spanning urban upstream (L1-2), urban core (L3-5), and urban downstream zones (L6) (Figure 1). Targeted droplet digital PCR (ddPCR) was used to quantify relevant ARGs, including Gram-positives (mecA and vanA), Gram-negatives beta-lactamases (CTX-M and SHV), AmpC-type β-lactamase (CMY), and Carbapenemase (KPC, NDM, VIM, IMP, and OXA-48), tetracycline (tetW) and Polymyxin-resistant (MCR-1). Physicochemical parameters and fecal indicator bacteria were measured concurrently to contextualize microbial contamination. Spatial and temporal trends in ARG abundance and composition were evaluated using non-parametric statistical analyses. Results: ARGs were widely detected across the watershed, with particularly high abundances of tetW, CMY, TEM, and multiple Gram-negative carbapenemase genes, including KPC, OXA-48, and VIM. The plasmid-mediated colistin resis- tance gene mcr-1 was also detected at multiple sites, highlighting the envi- ronmental presence of resistance determinants associated with last-resort antimicrobials (Figure 2). ARG abundances generally increased from urban upstream to urban downstream locations, likely reflecting cumula- tive inputs from domestic wastewater, healthcare facilities, and densely populated areas. Although ARG loads peaked within the urban core, elevated resistance signals remained detectable in downstream urban edge regions (Figure 3). In contrast to largely compliant physicochemical con- ditions, fecal indicator bacteria revealed pervasive microbial contamina- tion across urban sites. Conclusions: Our findings demonstrate extensive resistome contamination within an urban river system, encom- passing both environmental and clinically important ARGs. The spatial accumulation of resistance signals downstream and the detection of coli- stin resistance genes underscore the role of river ecosystem as conduits linking human activity to broader environmental AMR dissemination. analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to develop a tool for infection preventionists (IPs) to stratify suspect measles cases by risk level, thereby supporting decisions to prioritize or defer active intervention while awaiting test results.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study population included patients tested for measles during the implementation period, with a production cohort of 56 patients tested for measles since the tool's deployment.
analysis.methods: A two-dimensional risk matrix was developed incorporating both epidemiological and clinical risk factors, each scored numerically based on yes or no questions. The sum of both categories was used to assign a final risk level. Descriptive statistics were used to summarize the distribution of risk categories and outcomes. Firth’s logistic regression was used to evaluate the association between clinical or epidemiological risk score and measles diagnosis.
analysis.main_results: Among the 56 patients tested for measles, 10.7% (n=6) were categorized as high risk, 32.1% (n=18) as medium, and 57.1% (n=32) as low risk. Four of the 56 patients were positive for measles, with 3 categorized as high-risk and 1 as medium risk. The low-risk category had an NPV of 1, indicating that all low-risk patients tested negative.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The Measles Exposure Response Risk Matrix effectively stratified cases and supported IP prioritization efforts, transitioning clinical and epidemiologic risk scores from arbitrary assignment to validated metrics confirmed by statistical analysis.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The tool supports rapid, evidence-based actions by infection prevention teams, particularly in settings with rising measles incidence, enabling efficient resource allocation and prioritization of interventions.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on a single tool's application and the potential for unmeasured confounding factors. The evidence is moderate, as the findings are based on a single cohort and statistical analysis.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to develop a tool for infection preventionists to stratify suspect measles cases by risk level, supporting decisions on intervention prioritization. The tool, a two-dimensional risk matrix, incorporated epidemiological and clinical risk factors, each scored numerically. It was applied to 56 patients tested for measles, with 10.7% categorized as high risk, 32.1% as medium, and 57.1% as low risk. Four patients tested positive for measles, with 3 in the high-risk category and 1 in the medium-risk category. The low-risk category had an NPV of 1, indicating all low-risk patients tested negative. The matrix effectively stratified cases, transitioning risk scores from arbitrary to validated metrics. The findings suggest the tool can support efficient resource allocation and prioritization of interventions in settings with rising measles incidence. However, the study is limited by its reliance on a single tool and potential unmeasured confounding factors, resulting in moderate evidence strength.

full_text: Presentation Type: Poster Presentation Subject Category: Surveillance Abstract ID: 196 Breakthrough COVID-19 Infections Among Vaccinated Residents of VA Community Living Centers Brandon Smith1 EST Healthcare water management programs (WMPs) have historically emphasized the control of Legionella pneumophila, largely due to its estab- lished role in Legionnaires’ disease outbreaks. However, healthcare water systems harbor a wide range of opportunistic premise plumbing pathogens (OPPPs), including nontuberculous mycobacteria (NTM), Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Acinetobacter baumannii, Stenotrophomonas maltophilia, and Burkholderia cepacia complex. These organisms exhibit distinct eco- logical preferences and persistence mechanisms that vary by system type. In this study, we analyze microbiological testing data from more than 200,000 healthcare-associated water system samples collected since September 2019, comparing pathogen positivity across ice machines, gen- eral potable water, and cooling towers. Results demonstrate substantial variability in pathogen positivity by system type, with NTM showing mark- edly higher positivity in ice machines and potable water systems (relative to traditional indicator organisms). Legionella pneumophila positivity was highest in cooling towers but substantially lower in potable water. These findings indicate that uniform, organism-agnostic surveillance strategies are insufficient and that WMPs must be selectively designed based on sys- tem type, exposure route, and patient risk. Adopting site-specific, organ- ism-selective monitoring frameworks may significantly improve infection prevention efforts in healthcare settings. S1):s185 doi:10.1017/ash.2026.10727 Presentation Type: Poster Presentation Subject Category: Surveillance Abstract ID: 226 Patterns and Gaps in Mpox Vaccination at NYC Health + Hospitals, a Large Urban Safety Net Health System in New York City, 2022-2025 Shatha AlShanqeeti1, Gaayathri Krishnan2, Crisanta Simon, Jonathan Baghdadi1, Katherine Goodman1, Gregory Schrank1, Jessica Holman, Lisa Pineles3, Cassie Cunningham Goedken4, Christine Firestone, KC Coffey5, Westyn Branch-Elliman, Surbhi Leekha6, Anthony Harris1 and Daniel Morgan1 1University of Maryland School of Medicine; 2University of Maryland; 3University of Maryland, Baltimore; 4Center for Access & Delivery Research & Evaluation (CADRE), Iowa City Veterans Affairs Health Care System, Iowa City, IA, USA; 5Massachusetts General Hospital and 6University of Maryland Baltimore Background: Hospital onset bacteremia and fungemia (HOB) is under development as a Center for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) auto- mated digital quality measure. We evaluated the use of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) in assessing attribution and preventability of HOB. Methods This is a retrospective cohort study of hospitalized patients with positive blood cultures at 11 US Veterans Affairs (VA) hospitals. We included a random sample of positive blood cultures collected after day 3 of admission where admission date is day 1. GenAI (OpenAI GPT- 4o) was prompted to provide the most likely source and adjudicate the pre- ventability of HOB using standardized prompts and clinical data (GenAI). IP experts used GenAI output to provide GenAI-assisted determinations of source and preventability of HOB (IP-AI). HOB event preventability was rated by IP expert using a 6-point Likert scale, responses were combined to 3 categories for analysis. We compared initial GenAI with IP-AI determi- nations of source and preventability. A separate human-only review by a different IP expert was performed (IP-alone) on a random subset to com- pare time required for review. Results We included 52 HOB events for IP- AI and a subset of 21 for IP-alone. Enterobacterales were the most common organisms (22/52, 42%) followed by Staphylococcus aureus (9/52, 17%). Median duration to HOB event was 12 (IQR 5 – 31) days. GenAI most commonly attributed bacteremia to gastrointestinal (GI) (14/52, 26.9%), followed by genitourinary (GU) (12/52, 23%), central line (CLABSI) (8/ 52, 15%), and skin and soft tissue infections (SSTI) (7/52, 14%) sources (Figure 1). IP-AI determination of source agreed with GenAI source in 67% (35/52) of cases. Most agreement between IP-AI and GenAI occurred when HOB was attributed to a bone and joint infection (2/2, 100%), fol- lowed by GI source (13/14, 93%), SSTI (5/7, 71%), and GU source (7/12, 58%). Most disagreements (17/52, 33%) occurred when IP-AI attribution was to an unknown source (5/17, 29%) or blood culture contamination (3/ 17, 18%). GenAI adjudication of preventability matched IP-AI adjudica- tion in 20/52 (39%). The median time to complete an IP-AI review was 11.5 (IQR 6 – 20.5) minutes compared to a median of 25 (IQR 13 – 33) minutes for IP-alone. Conclusion IP experts often agreed with GenAI for source of HOB but disagreed with its preventability. GenAI rarely acknowledged unknown source. Using GenAI for HOB detection is faster than human review but must account for differences in preventability. Antimicrobial Stewardship & Healthcare Epidemiology 2026;6(Suppl. analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to evaluate the use of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) in assessing the attribution and preventability of hospital-onset bacteremia and fungemia (HOB) events, addressing the need for efficient and accurate methods to identify sources and preventability in healthcare settings.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A retrospective cohort study was conducted at 11 US Veterans Affairs (VA) hospitals, including a random sample of positive blood cultures collected after day 3 of admission where admission date is day 1. The study included 52 HOB events for IP-AI and a subset of 21 for IP-alone.
analysis.methods: GenAI (OpenAI GPT-4o) was prompted to provide the most likely source and adjudicate the preventability of HOB using standardized prompts and clinical data. IP experts used GenAI output to provide GenAI-assisted determinations of source and preventability, and a separate human-only review by a different IP expert was performed on a random subset to compare time required for review.
analysis.main_results: GenAI most commonly attributed HOB to gastrointestinal (GI) sources (26.9%), followed by genitourinary (GU) (23%), central line (CLABSI) (15%), and skin and soft tissue infections (SSTI) (14%). IP-AI determination of source agreed with GenAI in 67% (35/52) of cases, with most agreement when HOB was attributed to bone and joint infections, GI sources, SSTI, and GU sources. The median time to complete an IP-AI review was 11.5 (IQR 6 – 20.5) minutes compared to a median of 25 (IQR 13 – 33) minutes for IP-alone.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings indicate that IP experts often agree with GenAI for the source of HOB but disagree with its preventability assessment, highlighting the potential of GenAI to expedite HOB source identification while emphasizing the need for human oversight in preventability judgments.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results suggest that integrating GenAI into HOB surveillance could enhance the speed of source identification, potentially improving infection prevention strategies in healthcare settings, although preventability assessments require expert validation.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on a single AI model and a relatively small sample size, which may affect the generalizability of findings. The evidence is moderate in strength due to the retrospective design and potential biases in AI interpretation.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the use of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) in assessing the attribution and preventability of hospital-onset bacteremia and fungemia (HOB) events. A retrospective cohort study was conducted at 11 US Veterans Affairs (VA) hospitals, analyzing 52 HOB events using GenAI-assisted methods and comparing them with human expert assessments. GenAI most commonly attributed HOB to gastrointestinal sources, followed by genitourinary, central line, and skin and soft tissue infections. IP-AI agreed with GenAI in 67% of cases, with higher agreement for certain sources. The median time for IP-AI review was significantly shorter than for human-only review. While GenAI showed promise in expediting source identification, its preventability assessments were less consistent with expert opinions. The study highlights the potential of AI in HOB surveillance but underscores the need for human validation in critical areas. The evidence is moderate in strength due to the study's design and potential biases.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在评估生成型人工智能(GenAI)在评估医院获得性菌血症和真菌血症(HOB)事件的归因和可预防性方面的应用,以应对医疗环境中快速且准确识别来源和可预防性的需求。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 回顾性队列研究研究在11家美国退伍军人事务管理局(VA)医院进行,纳入了入院第3天之后采集的阳性血培养样本(入院日为第1天)。该研究共纳入52例IP-AI事件,其中21例为IP-alone的子集。
elements_zh.methods: GenAI(OpenAI GPT-4o)被提示提供最可能的HOB来源,并根据标准化提示和临床数据判断其可预防性。IP专家利用GenAI的输出结果,对HOB的来源和可预防性进行GenAI辅助判断,同时对随机选取的子集进行了单独的人类评审,以比较评审所需时间。
elements_zh.main_results: GenAI最常将HOB归因于胃肠道(GI)来源(26.9%),其次是泌尿生殖系统(GU)(23%)、中心静脉导管相关血流感染(CLABSI)(15%)以及皮肤和软组织感染(SSTI)(14%)。在IP-AI对HOB来源的判断中,有67%(35/52)的案例与GenAI一致,当HOB归因于骨关节感染、胃肠道来源、皮肤和软组织感染以及泌尿生殖系统来源时,一致性最高。完成IP-AI评审的中位时间是11.5分钟(IQR 6 – 20.5),而IP-alone的中位时间是25分钟(IQR 13 – 33)。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 这些发现表明,IP专家通常同意GenAI对HOB来源的判断,但对其可预防性评估存在分歧,突显了GenAI在加速HOB来源识别方面的潜力,同时强调了在可预防性判断中需要人类监督的重要性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果表明,将GenAI整合到HOB 监测中可能有助于加快来源识别,从而潜在地改善医疗环境中的感染预防策略,尽管可预防性评估仍需要专家验证。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究的局限性在于依赖单一AI模型和相对较小的样本量,这可能影响研究结果的普遍适用性。由于研究设计为回顾性,且AI解释可能存在偏倚,因此证据强度中等。

analysis_en.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to evaluate the use of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) in assessing the attribution and preventability of hospital-onset bacteremia and fungemia (HOB) events, addressing the need for efficient and accurate methods to identify sources and preventability in healthcare settings.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: A retrospective cohort study was conducted at 11 US Veterans Affairs (VA) hospitals, including a random sample of positive blood cultures collected after day 3 of admission where admission date is day 1. The study included 52 HOB events for IP-AI and a subset of 21 for IP-alone.
analysis_en.methods: GenAI (OpenAI GPT-4o) was prompted to provide the most likely source and adjudicate the preventability of HOB using standardized prompts and clinical data. IP experts used GenAI output to provide GenAI-assisted determinations of source and preventability, and a separate human-only review by a different IP expert was performed on a random subset to compare time required for review.
analysis_en.main_results: GenAI most commonly attributed HOB to gastrointestinal (GI) sources (26.9%), followed by genitourinary (GU) (23%), central line (CLABSI) (15%), and skin and soft tissue infections (SSTI) (14%). IP-AI determination of source agreed with GenAI in 67% (35/52) of cases, with most agreement when HOB was attributed to bone and joint infections, GI sources, SSTI, and GU sources. The median time to complete an IP-AI review was 11.5 (IQR 6 – 20.5) minutes compared to a median of 25 (IQR 13 – 33) minutes for IP-alone.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings indicate that IP experts often agree with GenAI for the source of HOB but disagree with its preventability assessment, highlighting the potential of GenAI to expedite HOB source identification while emphasizing the need for human oversight in preventability judgments.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results suggest that integrating GenAI into HOB surveillance could enhance the speed of source identification, potentially improving infection prevention strategies in healthcare settings, although preventability assessments require expert validation.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on a single AI model and a relatively small sample size, which may affect the generalizability of findings. The evidence is moderate in strength due to the retrospective design and potential biases in AI interpretation.

source_body_en: In this study, we analyze microbiological testing data from more than 200,000 healthcare-associated water system samples collected since September 2019, comparing pathogen positivity across ice machines, gen- eral potable water, and cooling towers. Results demonstrate substantial variability in pathogen positivity by system type, with NTM showing mark- edly higher positivity in ice machines and potable water systems (relative to traditional indicator organisms). These findings indicate that uniform, organism-agnostic surveillance strategies are insufficient and that WMPs must be selectively designed based on sys- tem type, exposure route, and patient risk. Methods This is a retrospective cohort study of hospitalized patients with positive blood cultures at 11 US Veterans Affairs (VA) hospitals. A separate human-only review by a different IP expert was performed (IP-alone) on a random subset to com- pare time required for review. Results We included 52 HOB events for IP- AI and a subset of 21 for IP-alone. The median time to complete an IP-AI review was 11.5 (IQR 6 – 20.5) minutes compared to a median of 25 (IQR 13 – 33) minutes for IP-alone. Conclusion IP experts often agreed with GenAI for source of HOB but disagreed with its preventability.
